meanings_zh: adj. 不同的 | adj. 各不相同的；各种的
definition_en: not the same | used to describe several separate people, things, or types
example1_en: Each student has a different style.
example1_zh: 每个学生都有不同风格。
example2_en: Students from different cultural backgrounds can contribute valuable perspectives to classroom discussions about global issues.
example2_zh: 来自不同文化背景的学生能为课堂上的全球议题讨论提供宝贵的视角。
collocations: different from｜与……不同 ; different perspectives｜不同视角 ; completely different｜完全不同
tip_zh: 与……不同常用different from，适合正式写作。

meanings_zh: n. 交谈
definition_en: an informal talk
example1_en: They had a long conversation about books.
example1_zh: 他们就书籍进行了长时间交谈。
example2_en: Regular conversation with fluent speakers helps language learners develop confidence and improve their listening skills.
example2_zh: 经常与语言流利的人交谈有助于语言学习者建立信心并提高听力。
collocations: have a conversation｜交谈 ; start a conversation｜开始交谈 ; a conversation about｜关于……的谈话
tip_zh: 与某人谈某事：have a conversation with某人about某事。

meanings_zh: n. 例子 | n. 榜样
definition_en: something that shows a rule | A person or action that others can learn from or copy
example1_en: Give an example to support your idea.
example1_zh: 举一个例子支持你的观点。
example2_en: Public buildings can set an example by using renewable energy and reducing unnecessary water consumption.
example2_zh: 公共建筑可以通过使用可再生能源和减少不必要的用水来树立榜样。
collocations: for example｜例如 ; give an example｜举例 ; set an example｜树立榜样 ; a typical example｜典型例子
tip_zh: for example用于举例；set an example意为树立榜样。

meanings_zh: v. 同意 | v. 商定；答应
definition_en: to have the same opinion | Decide something together or promise to do something
example1_en: I agree with your suggestion.
example2_en: Most researchers agree that regular physical activity can improve both mental health and academic performance.
example2_zh: 大多数研究人员认为，经常运动可以改善心理健康和学业表现。
collocations: agree with someone｜同意某人的观点 ; agree on a plan｜就计划达成一致 ; agree to do something｜答应做某事 ; agree to a proposal｜同意一项提议
tip_zh: 同意某人用with；商定某事用on；答应做用to do。

meanings_zh: adj. 困难的 | adj. 难相处的；难应付的
definition_en: hard to do | Not easy to please, manage, or deal with.
example1_en: The question is difficult.
example2_en: Many graduates find it difficult to secure stable employment without previous experience in their chosen field.
example2_zh: 许多毕业生发现，如果没有所选领域的工作经验，就很难找到稳定的工作。
collocations: a difficult decision｜艰难的决定 ; difficult to understand｜难以理解 ; a difficult customer｜难应付的顾客
tip_zh: 常用find it difficult to do，勿把difficulty当形容词。

meanings_zh: v. 描述
definition_en: to say what something is like
example1_en: Can you describe the scene in detail?
example1_zh: 你能详细描述那个场景吗？
example2_en: The report describes how access to public parks influences physical activity among residents of crowded cities.
example2_zh: 该报告描述了公共公园的可达性如何影响人口密集城市居民的体育活动。
collocations: describe something in detail｜详细描述某事物 ; describe something as｜把某事物形容为 ; describe a process｜描述一个过程
tip_zh: 说describe something to someone，不说describe someone something。

meanings_zh: v. 设计 | n. 设计；设计方案 | n. 装饰图案
definition_en: to plan how something looks or works | the planning of something's appearance or function, or its plan | a decorative pattern on an object or surface
example1_en: They will design a new school logo.
example1_zh: 他们将设计一个新的校徽。
example2_en: Cities should design public spaces that encourage social interaction while remaining accessible to people with disabilities.
example2_zh: 城市应设计既能促进社交互动、又方便残障人士使用的公共空间。
collocations: design a building｜设计建筑 ; be designed to do something｜旨在做某事 ; graphic design｜平面设计 ; interior design｜室内设计
tip_zh: be designed to do表示“旨在做……”。

meanings_zh: n. 能力；才能
definition_en: skill or power to do something
example1_en: Language ability grows with practice.
example1_zh: 语言能力随练习而增长。
example2_en: Regular reading can strengthen children's ability to understand complex ideas and express their own views clearly.
example2_zh: 经常阅读可以增强儿童理解复杂概念和清晰表达自身观点的能力。
collocations: the ability to learn｜学习能力 ; develop an ability｜培养一种能力 ; academic ability｜学业能力 ; natural ability｜天赋
tip_zh: 表示“做某事的能力”用ability to do。

meanings_zh: n. 距离 | n. 疏远；隔阂 | v. 使疏远；撇清关系
definition_en: space between two points | A lack of emotional closeness between people | To separate yourself from someone, something, or their views
example1_en: Keep a safe distance from the fire.
example2_en: Reducing the distance between residential areas and workplaces could lower transport emissions and improve urban quality of life.
example2_zh: 缩短住宅区与工作地点之间的距离，可以减少交通排放并改善城市生活质量。
collocations: walking distance｜步行可达的距离 ; in the distance｜在远处 ; keep your distance｜保持距离 ; distance yourself from｜与……划清界限
tip_zh: in the distance指在远处；at a distance指隔一段距离。

meanings_zh: n. 精力；能源 | n. 能量；能源
definition_en: power to work; power source | Power used to produce heat, movement, light, or electricity
example1_en: Young people have lots of energy.
example2_en: Investing in renewable energy can reduce dependence on fossil fuels while creating new employment opportunities.
example2_zh: 投资可再生能源可以减少对化石燃料的依赖，同时创造新的就业机会。
collocations: full of energy｜精力充沛 ; renewable energy｜可再生能源 ; energy consumption｜能源消耗 ; save energy｜节约能源
tip_zh: 表示精力或能源时通常不可数，不说 an energy。

meanings_zh: n. 比赛；竞争 | n. 比赛；竞赛
definition_en: a contest | An organised event in which people try to win.
example1_en: She won first prize in the competition.
example1_zh: 她在比赛中获得一等奖。
example2_en: Competition between businesses can lower prices, but effective regulation is needed to protect consumers from unfair practices.
example2_zh: 企业间的竞争可以降低价格，但仍需有效监管来保护消费者免受不公平商业行为的侵害。
collocations: fierce competition｜激烈竞争 ; competition for jobs｜求职竞争 ; enter a competition｜参加比赛 ; win a competition｜赢得比赛
tip_zh: 表示竞争通常不可数；表示一场比赛时可数。

meanings_zh: v. 讨论 | v. 论述
definition_en: to talk about | to examine a subject in speech or writing
example1_en: Let's discuss the plan after lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭后我们讨论一下计划。
example2_en: Students should discuss different solutions before deciding how to reduce waste on their campus.
example2_zh: 学生应先讨论不同的解决办法，再决定如何减少校园垃圾。
collocations: discuss a problem｜讨论问题 ; discuss something with someone｜与某人讨论某事 ; discuss in detail｜详细讨论
tip_zh: 直接接讨论内容：discuss sth，不加about。

meanings_zh: v. 发现
definition_en: to find for the first time
example1_en: Scientists discover new planets every year.
example1_zh: 科学家每年都发现新行星。
example2_en: Scientists may discover new ways to treat diseases by studying plants in tropical forests.
example2_zh: 科学家可能通过研究热带森林中的植物，发现治疗疾病的新方法。
collocations: discover a cure｜发现疗法 ; discover a new species｜发现新物种 ; discover the truth｜发现真相
tip_zh: discover发现原本存在的事物；invent创造新事物。

meanings_zh: adj. 电的 | adj. 令人激动的
definition_en: using electricity | Full of excitement and energy.
example1_en: electric cars produce less smoke.
example1_zh: 电动汽车产生更少烟雾。
example2_en: Electric buses can reduce urban air pollution, especially when their power comes from renewable sources.
example2_zh: 电动公交车可以减少城市空气污染，尤其是在使用可再生能源供电时。
collocations: electric car｜电动汽车 ; electric current｜电流 ; electric shock｜电击 ; electric atmosphere｜热烈的气氛
tip_zh: 电动设备多用electric；电气系统多用electrical。

meanings_zh: adj. 方便的 | adj. 附近的；便于到达的
definition_en: easy to use or reach | Situated close to somewhere you need to reach.
example1_en: Online payment is convenient.
example2_en: Online learning offers a convenient way for working adults to develop skills without travelling to a campus.
example2_zh: 在线学习为在职成年人提供了无需前往校园就能提升技能的便捷途径。
collocations: a convenient time｜合适的时间 ; convenient for someone｜对某人方便 ; a convenient location｜便利的位置 ; a convenient way to｜做……的便捷方式
tip_zh: 说 It is convenient for me，不说 I am convenient。

meanings_zh: adj. 积极的；活跃的 | adj. 运作中的；起作用的 | adj. 主动语态的
definition_en: busy doing things | currently working or producing an effect | describing a verb whose subject performs the action
example1_en: Stay active after school.
example2_en: Schools should encourage an active lifestyle to improve students' physical health and overall wellbeing.
example2_zh: 学校应鼓励积极运动的生活方式，以改善学生的身体健康和整体身心状态。
collocations: stay active｜保持活力 ; an active lifestyle｜积极运动的生活方式 ; play an active role｜发挥积极作用 ; active ingredient｜有效成分
tip_zh: active指积极活动或参与；不等于表示乐观的positive。

meanings_zh: v. 依靠；取决于 | v. 依赖；信赖
definition_en: to need support; to be decided by | to need or trust someone or something for support
example1_en: Success may depend on hard work.
example2_en: Many rural communities depend on reliable public transport to access healthcare, education, and employment opportunities.
example2_zh: 许多农村社区依靠可靠的公共交通来获得医疗、教育和就业机会。
collocations: depend on｜取决于；依赖 ; depend heavily on｜严重依赖 ; depend on someone to do something｜指望某人做某事
tip_zh: 常接on或upon；It depends意为“看情况”。

meanings_zh: v. 发展；培养 | v. 开发；研制 | v. 逐渐出现；患上
definition_en: to grow or improve | to create a new product, method, or idea | to begin to have a condition, problem, or feeling
example1_en: Reading helps develop your vocabulary.
example1_zh: 阅读有助于培养词汇量。
example2_en: Governments should fund research to develop affordable technologies that address water shortages in rural communities.
example2_zh: 政府应资助研究，开发价格可负担的技术，以解决农村社区的缺水问题。
collocations: develop skills｜培养技能 ; develop a habit｜养成习惯 ; develop new technology｜开发新技术 ; develop symptoms｜出现症状
tip_zh: 可及物也可不及物：develop skills；skills develop。

meanings_zh: n. 差异 | n. 分歧；意见不合 | n. 差额；差值
definition_en: the way things are not the same | A disagreement between people or groups | The amount by which one quantity exceeds another
example1_en: Age makes little difference in friendship.
example1_zh: 年龄在友谊中几乎没有差异。
example2_en: Understanding cultural differences can help international students adapt more successfully to life in a new country.
example2_zh: 了解文化差异有助于留学生更顺利地适应新国家的生活。
collocations: the difference between｜……之间的区别 ; make a difference｜产生影响 ; a significant difference｜显著差异 ; settle differences｜解决分歧
tip_zh: 比较两者用the difference between A and B。

meanings_zh: adj. 有帮助的 | adj. 乐于助人的
definition_en: useful | Willing to help other people.
example1_en: Your notes were very helpful.
example2_en: Clear feedback is particularly helpful for students who are learning to organise their ideas in academic essays.
example2_zh: 对于正在学习如何组织学术论文思路的学生来说，清晰的反馈尤其有帮助。
collocations: helpful advice｜有用的建议 ; helpful information｜有用的信息 ; helpful staff｜乐于助人的员工 ; find something helpful｜觉得某物有帮助
tip_zh: helpful可形容事物有用，也可形容人乐于助人。

meanings_zh: n. 疾病
definition_en: an illness
example1_en: Clean water helps prevent disease.
example1_zh: 干净的水有助于预防疾病。
example2_en: Access to clean drinking water can significantly reduce the spread of infectious diseases in vulnerable communities.
example2_zh: 获得清洁饮用水可以显著减少传染病在脆弱社区中的传播。
collocations: heart disease｜心脏病 ; infectious diseases｜传染病 ; prevent disease｜预防疾病 ; the spread of disease｜疾病传播
tip_zh: 重音在第二音节；泛指疾病可不加冠词。

meanings_zh: v. 取消 | v. 抵消
definition_en: to stop a planned event | To balance an opposing effect so neither changes the result.
example1_en: They had to cancel the trip because of rain.
example1_zh: 因为下雨他们不得不取消旅行。
example2_en: Improved energy efficiency may cancel out some environmental benefits if it encourages people to consume more.
example2_zh: 如果能源效率提高促使人们增加消费，就可能抵消部分环境效益。
collocations: cancel a booking｜取消预订 ; cancel a flight｜取消航班 ; cancel out｜抵消
tip_zh: 英式过去式cancelled，美式常用canceled；抵消用out。

meanings_zh: adj. 国际的 | n. 国际比赛；国家队选手
definition_en: between countries | A match between countries, or a player representing a country.
example1_en: English is an international language.
example2_en: International cooperation is essential for tackling environmental problems that extend beyond the borders of individual countries.
example2_zh: 国际合作对于解决超越单个国家边界的环境问题至关重要。
collocations: international trade｜国际贸易 ; international cooperation｜国际合作 ; an international flight｜国际航班 ; international students｜国际学生
tip_zh: international涉及多国；domestic指国内的。

meanings_zh: n. 方向；指导 | n. 路线指引；使用说明 | n. 指导；管理
definition_en: the way to go; guidance | instructions explaining how to reach somewhere or do something | the control or guidance of an activity or group
example1_en: Ask for direction if you get lost.
example2_en: Government investment can influence the direction of technological development by supporting research into cleaner energy sources.
example2_zh: 政府投资可以通过支持清洁能源研究来影响技术发展的方向。
collocations: in the opposite direction｜朝相反方向 ; ask for directions｜问路 ; follow the directions｜遵照说明 ; under the direction of｜在……的指导下
tip_zh: 表示路线指引或操作说明时，通常用复数directions。

meanings_zh: adj. 令人惊奇的
definition_en: very surprising
example1_en: What an amazing view from the hill!
example1_zh: 山顶的景色多么令人惊奇！
example2_en: Recent medical research has produced amazing results, offering new hope to patients with previously untreatable conditions.
example2_zh: 近期医学研究取得了惊人的成果，为患有过去无法治疗的疾病的患者带来了新希望。
collocations: absolutely amazing｜极其精彩的 ; amazing results｜惊人的成果 ; an amazing experience｜一次奇妙的经历
tip_zh: amazing形容令人惊叹的事物；amazed形容人的感受。

meanings_zh: v. 接受；承认 | v. 承认；认可 | v. 承担；接受现实
definition_en: to take or agree to something offered | Recognize that something is true or valid | Take responsibility or stop resisting an unpleasant situation
example1_en: She decided to accept the job offer.
example1_zh: 她决定接受这份工作邀约。
example2_en: Governments must accept responsibility for ensuring that all children have access to basic education.
example2_zh: 政府必须承担责任，确保所有儿童都能接受基础教育。
collocations: accept an offer｜接受提议 ; accept responsibility｜承担责任 ; accept an invitation｜接受邀请 ; accept that｜承认……
tip_zh: 接受建议用accept；接受某物不等于仅仅收到receive。

meanings_zh: adj. 基本的 | adj. 简单的；无额外设施的
definition_en: simple and most important | Having only necessary features, without anything extra.
example1_en: Learn the basic rules first.
example2_en: Governments should ensure that all citizens have access to basic healthcare, regardless of their income.
example2_zh: 政府应确保所有公民都能获得基本医疗服务，不论其收入如何。
collocations: basic skills｜基本技能 ; basic needs｜基本需求 ; basic knowledge｜基础知识 ; basic principles｜基本原则
tip_zh: 名词“基础知识”用复数 the basics。

meanings_zh: v. 允许 | v. 使可能；容许 | v. 留出；预留
definition_en: to let someone do something | to make something possible | to provide enough time or resources for something
example1_en: Parents should allow kids to make choices.
example1_zh: 父母应允许孩子做选择。
example2_en: Flexible working arrangements allow employees to balance their professional responsibilities with family commitments more effectively.
example2_zh: 灵活的工作安排使员工能够更有效地兼顾工作职责与家庭义务。
collocations: allow someone to do something｜允许某人做某事 ; allow enough time｜留出足够时间 ; allow for delays｜考虑到可能的延误
tip_zh: 用allow sb to do；无宾语时可用allow doing。

meanings_zh: v. 破坏；摧毁 | v. 彻底破坏；使丧失
definition_en: to ruin completely | To completely end something valuable, such as trust or hope.
example1_en: Fire can destroy a whole forest.
example2_en: Uncontrolled urban expansion can destroy natural habitats and threaten the survival of species that depend on them.
example2_zh: 不受控制的城市扩张会摧毁自然栖息地，威胁依赖这些栖息地的物种生存。
collocations: destroy habitats｜摧毁栖息地 ; destroy evidence｜销毁证据 ; destroy confidence｜摧毁信心 ; completely destroy｜彻底摧毁
tip_zh: destroy比damage程度重，通常指彻底毁坏。

meanings_zh: n. 程度；学位 | n. 程度 | n. 度；度数
definition_en: level; a university title | the amount or level of something | a unit used to measure temperature or angles
example1_en: To some degree, luck plays a role.
example1_zh: 在某种程度上，运气起作用。
example2_en: Although a university degree can improve employment prospects, practical experience remains highly valuable in many industries.
example2_zh: 虽然大学学位能改善就业前景，但实践经验在许多行业仍然十分重要。
collocations: a degree in economics｜经济学学位 ; a bachelor's degree｜学士学位 ; to some degree｜在某种程度上 ; degrees Celsius｜摄氏度
tip_zh: 某专业的学位用a degree in；程度义常见to some degree。

meanings_zh: n. 行为 | n. 运行特性；反应方式
definition_en: the way someone acts | the way a substance or system acts under particular conditions
example1_en: Good behavior is expected in class.
example1_zh: 课堂上期望有良好行为。
example2_en: Schools can encourage responsible behavior by giving students meaningful opportunities to participate in decisions affecting their community.
example2_zh: 学校可以让学生有实质性机会参与影响其社区的决策，以此鼓励负责任的行为。
collocations: good behavior｜良好行为 ; consumer behavior｜消费者行为 ; animal behavior｜动物行为 ; patterns of behavior｜行为模式
tip_zh: 美式拼写；英式为behaviour。通常不可数。

meanings_zh: adj. 可获得的；有空的 | adj. 有空的
definition_en: able to be used or free | Not busy and able to meet or help someone.
example1_en: Is the book available in the library?
example2_en: Affordable housing should be available to all residents, regardless of their income or employment status.
example2_zh: 所有居民都应能获得负担得起的住房，不论其收入或就业状况如何。
collocations: readily available｜容易获得的 ; available to everyone｜人人都可获得的 ; available for use｜可供使用的 ; make something available｜使某物可供使用
tip_zh: available to接使用者；available for接用途。

meanings_zh: adj. 仔细的；小心的 | adj. 仔细的；细致的
definition_en: taking care to avoid mistakes | giving close attention to details
example1_en: Be careful when you cross the road.
example2_en: Careful planning can help cities expand public transport while keeping construction costs under control.
example2_zh: 周密的规划可以帮助城市扩展公共交通，同时控制建设成本。
collocations: be careful with｜小心对待 ; careful planning｜周密规划 ; careful consideration｜慎重考虑 ; careful analysis｜细致分析
tip_zh: be careful with后接物；be careful to后接动词。

meanings_zh: n. 建议
definition_en: an opinion about what to do
example1_en: Thank you for your useful advice.
example2_en: Schools should provide practical career advice so that students can make informed decisions about their future.
example2_zh: 学校应提供实用的职业建议，让学生能够对自己的未来作出明智决定。
collocations: give advice｜提供建议 ; seek advice｜寻求建议 ; follow advice｜听从建议 ; a piece of advice｜一条建议
tip_zh: 不可数，不用an advice；动词advise末尾读/z/。

meanings_zh: adj. 优秀的
definition_en: very good
example1_en: She did an excellent job.
example2_en: Excellent public transport can reduce car dependence and make cities more accessible to all residents.
example2_zh: 优质的公共交通可以减少人们对汽车的依赖，让所有居民出行更便利。
collocations: excellent service｜优质服务 ; excellent results｜优异成绩 ; excellent opportunity｜绝佳机会
tip_zh: 已含“极好”之意，通常不用very修饰。

meanings_zh: n. 决定
definition_en: a choice made
example1_en: Making a decision can take time.
example2_en: Governments should base every major transport decision on reliable evidence and consultation with the communities affected.
example2_zh: 政府的每项重大交通决策都应以可靠证据及与受影响社区的协商为基础。
collocations: make a decision｜作出决定 ; reach a decision｜达成决定 ; informed decision｜基于充分了解的决定 ; final decision｜最终决定
tip_zh: 作决定用make a decision，不用do。

meanings_zh: v. 出现；似乎 | v. 似乎；显得 | v. 登场；出庭
definition_en: to become visible; to seem | To seem to be a certain way. | To take part in a performance or attend court formally.
example1_en: A rainbow may appear after the rain.
example2_en: Online courses appear to offer greater flexibility, although some learners still prefer traditional classroom interaction.
example2_zh: 网络课程似乎提供了更大的灵活性，但一些学习者仍更喜欢传统课堂互动。
collocations: appear suddenly｜突然出现 ; appear to be｜似乎是 ; appear in court｜出庭
tip_zh: 表“似乎”可接形容词或to do；不能直接接宾语。

meanings_zh: adj. 当地的 | n. 当地人 | adj. 局部的
definition_en: of a particular area | a person who lives in a particular area | affecting only a limited part of something
example1_en: Buy local food when you can.
example2_en: Supporting local businesses can strengthen community ties and keep more money circulating within the regional economy.
example2_zh: 支持本地企业可以加强社区联系，并让更多资金在区域经济内部流通。
collocations: local community｜当地社区 ; local authorities｜地方当局 ; local residents｜当地居民 ; local anaesthetic｜局部麻醉药
tip_zh: 名词复数locals指当地人；locally是副词。

meanings_zh: v. 安排；整理 | v. 排列；整理
definition_en: to plan or put in order | Put things in a particular order or position.
example1_en: Please arrange the books on the shelf.
example1_zh: 请把书架上的书整理好。
example2_en: Schools can arrange visits to local businesses to help students understand the practical demands of different careers.
example2_zh: 学校可以安排学生参观当地企业，帮助他们了解不同职业的实际要求。
collocations: arrange a meeting｜安排会议 ; arrange to meet｜约好见面 ; arrange for someone to do something｜安排某人做某事 ; arrange flowers｜插花
tip_zh: 安排某人做某事用arrange for sb to do。

meanings_zh: v. 创造；创作 | v. 造成；引起
definition_en: to make something new | to cause a situation, feeling, or problem to develop
example1_en: Artists create works that move people.
example1_zh: 艺术家创作打动人心的作品。
example2_en: Investment in renewable energy can create jobs while reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels.
example2_zh: 投资可再生能源能创造就业机会，同时减少对进口化石燃料的依赖。
collocations: create opportunities｜创造机会 ; create jobs｜创造就业机会 ; create a problem｜造成问题 ; create a work of art｜创作艺术作品
tip_zh: create强调创造新事物，也可接problem表示造成问题。

meanings_zh: adj. 古代的；古老的 | adj. 非常古老的
definition_en: very old | having existed for a very long time
example1_en: We visited an ancient temple.
example2_en: Studying ancient civilisations helps researchers understand how early societies managed water, trade, and public health.
example2_zh: 研究古代文明有助于研究人员了解早期社会如何管理用水、贸易和公共卫生。
collocations: ancient history｜古代史 ; ancient civilisation｜古代文明 ; ancient ruins｜古代遗址 ; ancient monument｜古代历史遗迹
tip_zh: ancient强调年代久远，不宜代替一般的old。

meanings_zh: n. 数量；总额 | v. 总计；相当于
definition_en: a quantity | To total something or be equivalent to it.
example1_en: A large amount of rain fell last night.
example2_en: Reducing the amount of food wasted by households could significantly lower the environmental impact of food production.
example2_zh: 减少家庭食物浪费量可以显著降低食品生产对环境的影响。
collocations: a large amount of｜大量的 ; total amount｜总量；总额 ; amount to｜总计；相当于
tip_zh: amount of接不可数名词；动词常用amount to。

meanings_zh: adj. 现代的 | adj. 新式的；时髦的
definition_en: of present times | Using the latest ideas, methods, or styles.
example1_en: modern technology changes life.
example2_en: Modern technology allows students in remote areas to access educational resources previously available only in cities.
example2_zh: 现代技术让偏远地区的学生能够获取过去只有城市才有的教育资源。
collocations: modern society｜现代社会 ; modern technology｜现代技术 ; modern architecture｜现代建筑
tip_zh: modern强调现代或新式；不一定表示刚刚制造。

meanings_zh: adj. 确切的 | v. 强求；索取
definition_en: completely correct | Demand and obtain something, often through authority or force.
example1_en: What is the exact time?
example2_en: Researchers need exact measurements to determine whether changes in air quality are linked to new transport policies.
example2_zh: 研究人员需要精确的测量数据，以判断空气质量变化是否与新的交通政策有关。
collocations: exact location｜确切位置 ; exact amount｜准确数量 ; exact copy｜完全相同的复制品 ; exact a heavy toll｜造成惨重损失
tip_zh: exact强调分毫不差；副词形式为exactly。

meanings_zh: v. 比较 | v. 把……比作 | v. 比得上；可相比
definition_en: to look at differences and similarities | To describe something as similar to another thing. | To be as good as, or similar to, something else.
example1_en: Please compare these two essays carefully.
example1_zh: 请仔细比较这两篇文章。
example2_en: Researchers should compare the long-term costs of renewable energy with those of traditional power sources.
example2_zh: 研究人员应比较可再生能源与传统能源的长期成本。
collocations: compare prices｜比较价格 ; compare A with B｜将A与B比较 ; compare A to B｜将A比作B；比较A和B ; compare favourably with｜比起来不逊于
tip_zh: 比较可用with或to；表示比喻时通常用to。

meanings_zh: n. 设备
definition_en: tools needed for a task
example1_en: The lab has modern equipment.
example2_en: Schools need suitable laboratory equipment to give students practical experience and encourage an interest in science.
example2_zh: 学校需要合适的实验室设备，让学生获得实践经验并培养科学兴趣。
collocations: sports equipment｜体育器材 ; medical equipment｜医疗设备 ; safety equipment｜安全装备 ; a piece of equipment｜一件设备
tip_zh: 不可数；一件设备说a piece of equipment。

meanings_zh: v. 争论；主张 | v. 论证；主张
definition_en: to disagree in words; to claim | To give reasons supporting an opinion or position.
example1_en: They often argue about small things.
example2_en: Some researchers argue that affordable public transport is essential for reducing inequality in large cities.
example2_zh: 一些研究者认为，价格可负担的公共交通对于减少大城市中的不平等至关重要。
collocations: argue with someone｜与某人争论 ; argue about something｜就某事争论 ; argue that｜主张…… ; argue for｜据理支持
tip_zh: argue that常用于议论文，表示提出有理由的主张。

meanings_zh: n. 环境 | n. 生活或工作环境
definition_en: the natural world around us | The conditions and surroundings in which someone lives or works.
example1_en: We must protect the environment.
example2_en: A supportive learning environment can improve students' confidence and encourage them to participate more actively.
example2_zh: 支持性的学习环境能够增强学生的信心，鼓励他们更加积极地参与。
collocations: protect the environment｜保护环境 ; natural environment｜自然环境 ; working environment｜工作环境 ; learning environment｜学习环境
tip_zh: 泛指自然环境常用the environment。

meanings_zh: n. 描述
definition_en: words that tell what something is like
example1_en: Write a short description of your hometown.
example1_zh: 写一段对家乡的简短描述。
example2_en: A clear description of research methods allows other scientists to evaluate the reliability of a study.
example2_zh: 清楚描述研究方法，有助于其他科学家评估研究的可靠性。
collocations: a detailed description｜详细描述 ; give a description of｜描述 ; a job description｜岗位职责说明 ; an accurate description｜准确描述
tip_zh: 表示对某物的描述，用a description of，不用about。

meanings_zh: n. 原因；事业 | v. 导致；引起 | n. 事业；奋斗目标
definition_en: a reason; a movement to support | make something happen, especially something unpleasant | an aim or principle that people support and work towards
example1_en: Pollution is a major cause of illness.
example1_zh: 污染是疾病的一个主要原因。
example2_en: Heavy traffic is a major cause of air pollution in many rapidly growing urban areas.
example2_zh: 在许多快速发展的城市地区，繁忙的交通是空气污染的主要原因。
collocations: cause of｜……的原因 ; cause damage｜造成损害 ; root cause｜根本原因 ; a good cause｜公益事业
tip_zh: 名词常接of；动词可用cause sb to do sth。

meanings_zh: v. 决定 | v. 决定结果
definition_en: to make a choice | To determine the result of something.
example1_en: We must decide where to go.
example2_en: Governments must decide how to distribute limited resources between healthcare, education and public transport.
example2_zh: 政府必须决定如何在医疗、教育和公共交通之间分配有限资源。
collocations: decide to do something｜决定做某事 ; decide on｜选定 ; decide against｜决定不采用 ; decide the outcome｜决定结果
tip_zh: 用decide to do，不用decide doing。

meanings_zh: v. 避免 | v. 避开；躲避
definition_en: to keep away from | to stay away from someone or something
example1_en: Try to avoid eating too much sugar.
example2_en: Cities should improve public transport to avoid further increases in traffic congestion and air pollution.
example2_zh: 城市应改善公共交通，以避免交通拥堵和空气污染进一步加剧。
collocations: avoid doing something｜避免做某事 ; avoid mistakes｜避免犯错 ; avoid contact｜避免接触
tip_zh: 后接名词或动名词：avoid doing，不用to do。

meanings_zh: adj. 确定的；某一 | adj. 必然的；确定的 | adj. 某个；某些
definition_en: sure; particular | definitely going to happen | particular but not named or fully described
example1_en: I am certain that she will come.
example2_en: Certain types of public transport are more suitable for densely populated cities than rural areas.
example2_zh: 某些类型的公共交通更适合人口密集的城市，而非农村地区。
collocations: certain of｜对……有把握 ; certain to happen｜必然发生 ; make certain｜确保 ; certain types of｜某些类型的
tip_zh: 人作主语时，certain of表确信；certain to表必然。

meanings_zh: v. 连接；联系 | v. 联系；把…关联起来 | v. 与人建立良好关系
definition_en: to join or link | to recognize or establish a relationship between things | to develop a good relationship with someone
example1_en: Roads connect the village to the city.
example1_zh: 公路把村庄与城市连接起来。
example2_en: New rail services can connect rural communities with cities, improving access to education and employment.
example2_zh: 新的铁路服务可以连接农村社区与城市，让人们更容易获得教育和就业机会。
collocations: connect to the internet｜连接互联网 ; connect A with B｜把A与B联系起来 ; connect with people｜与人建立联系
tip_zh: 连接设备常用connect A to B。

meanings_zh: adj. 巨大的
definition_en: very big
example1_en: They made a huge effort.
example2_en: Investing in public transport could bring huge benefits to cities struggling with congestion and air pollution.
example2_zh: 对于饱受交通拥堵和空气污染困扰的城市，投资公共交通可以带来巨大益处。
collocations: huge amount｜巨大的数量 ; huge difference｜巨大差异 ; huge impact｜巨大影响 ; huge success｜巨大成功
tip_zh: 本身表示极大，常用absolutely huge加强语气。

meanings_zh: n. 事故；意外 | n. 意外；偶然发生的事
definition_en: an unexpected harmful event | Something that happens without being planned or intended.
example1_en: A car accident blocked the road.
example2_en: Better street lighting can reduce the risk of accidents involving cyclists and pedestrians at night.
example2_zh: 改善街道照明可以降低夜间涉及骑车人和行人的事故风险。
collocations: a road accident｜道路交通事故 ; by accident｜偶然；无意中 ; prevent accidents｜预防事故
tip_zh: by accident表示无意中，反义短语是on purpose。

meanings_zh: n. 机会；可能性 | n. 可能性 | n. 偶然；运气
definition_en: an opportunity | The likelihood that something will happen. | Events happening without planning or a predictable cause.
example1_en: This is your chance to speak up.
example2_en: Affordable training gives unemployed adults a chance to gain new skills and return to the workforce.
example2_zh: 费用可负担的培训让失业的成年人有机会掌握新技能，重返职场。
collocations: a chance to learn｜学习的机会 ; a good chance of｜很有可能 ; by chance｜偶然 ; take a chance｜冒险一试
tip_zh: 机会用chance to do；可能性常用chance of doing。

meanings_zh: n. 经验；经历 | n. 经历；体验 | v. 经历；感受
definition_en: knowledge from doing; an event lived through | something that happens to you or that you do | to have something happen to you or feel something
example1_en: Travel is a valuable experience.
example2_en: Work experience can help graduates develop practical skills that employers value alongside academic qualifications.
example2_zh: 工作经验能帮助毕业生培养实践技能，而雇主不仅重视学历，也看重这些技能。
collocations: gain experience｜积累经验 ; work experience｜工作经验 ; a rewarding experience｜有收获的经历 ; experience difficulties｜遇到困难
tip_zh: 表“经验”不可数；表具体“经历”可数。

meanings_zh: v. 庆祝 | v. 赞颂；颂扬
definition_en: to mark a happy event | To praise someone or something publicly.
example1_en: We will celebrate her birthday this weekend.
example1_zh: 我们这个周末会庆祝她的生日。
example2_en: Community festivals celebrate local traditions while giving residents opportunities to strengthen relationships with their neighbours.
example2_zh: 社区节庆活动在弘扬当地传统的同时，也让居民有机会增进邻里关系。
collocations: celebrate a birthday｜庆祝生日 ; celebrate an achievement｜庆祝一项成就 ; celebrate diversity｜赞颂多样性
tip_zh: 庆祝某事用celebrate；祝贺某人用congratulate。

meanings_zh: v. 使惊奇
definition_en: to surprise greatly
example1_en: The magic trick will amaze the children.
example1_zh: 这个魔术会让孩子们惊奇。
example2_en: Advances in medical technology continue to amaze researchers and offer new hope to patients with complex conditions.
example2_zh: 医疗技术的进步不断令研究人员惊叹，也为病情复杂的患者带来新的希望。
collocations: never cease to amaze｜始终令人惊叹 ; amaze an audience｜令观众惊叹 ; be amazed at｜对…感到惊奇
tip_zh: 人感到惊奇用amazed；事物令人惊奇用amazing。

meanings_zh: n. 内容 | adj. 满意的；知足的 | v. 使满足；使满意
definition_en: what is inside | Happy with what you have or with your situation | To make someone satisfied with what is available
example1_en: Check the content of the box carefully.
example2_en: Schools should teach students to evaluate online content critically rather than accepting every claim as reliable information.
example2_zh: 学校应教学生批判性地评估网络内容，而不是把每一种说法都当作可靠信息。
collocations: online content｜网络内容 ; sugar content｜含糖量 ; content with｜对……满意 ; content yourself with｜使自己满足于
tip_zh: 名词重音在前，形容词和动词在后；目录用contents。

meanings_zh: v. 集中（注意力） | v. 集中；聚集 | n. 浓缩物；浓缩液
definition_en: to focus attention | To bring things together in one place or direct efforts there. | A substance made stronger by removing water or other material.
example1_en: It is hard to concentrate in a noisy room.
example1_zh: 在嘈杂的房间里很难集中注意力。
example2_en: Governments should concentrate resources on preventive healthcare to reduce pressure on hospitals in the long term.
example2_zh: 政府应将资源集中于预防性医疗，以长期减轻医院的压力。
collocations: concentrate on a task｜专注于任务 ; concentrate resources on｜将资源集中于 ; fruit juice concentrate｜浓缩果汁
tip_zh: concentrate on后接名词或动名词，表示专注于。

meanings_zh: n. 通道；使用权 | n. 入口；通道 | v. 访问；获取；进入
definition_en: a way of entering or using | A way of reaching or entering a place. | Reach, enter, or obtain something, especially information on a computer.
example1_en: Students need access to the library.
example1_zh: 学生需要使用图书馆的权限。
example2_en: Affordable internet access enables rural students to benefit from a wider range of educational resources.
example2_zh: 价格可负担的互联网接入能让农村学生受益于更丰富的教育资源。
collocations: access to education｜受教育的机会 ; internet access｜互联网接入 ; gain access to｜获得使用或进入的机会 ; access information｜获取信息
tip_zh: 名词后接to；动词直接接宾语，不加to。

meanings_zh: n. 争论；论据 | n. 论点；论据
definition_en: a disagreement; a reason | A reason or set of reasons supporting an opinion.
example1_en: Their argument lasted for hours.
example1_zh: 他们的争论持续了几个小时。
example2_en: The strongest argument for public transport investment is its potential to reduce urban air pollution.
example2_zh: 支持投资公共交通最有力的论据是，它有望减少城市空气污染。
collocations: have an argument｜发生争吵 ; a convincing argument｜有说服力的论据 ; an argument for｜支持……的论据 ; an argument against｜反对……的论据
tip_zh: 争吵常接with或about；支持某观点用argument for。

meanings_zh: v. 减少 | n. 减少；减少量
definition_en: to become smaller in amount | A reduction in the size, number, or amount of something.
example1_en: Pollution may decrease if we use less plastic.
example1_zh: 如果我们少用塑料，污染可能会减少。
example2_en: Improved public transport could decrease traffic congestion and reduce air pollution in densely populated cities.
example2_zh: 改善公共交通可以缓解人口密集城市的交通拥堵，并减少空气污染。
collocations: a decrease in demand｜需求下降 ; decrease significantly｜显著减少 ; decrease by half｜减少一半 ; a steady decrease｜持续下降
tip_zh: 动词重音在后，名词/ˈdiːkriːs/重音在前。

meanings_zh: n. 错误 | n. 误差
definition_en: a mistake | the difference between a measured value and the true value
example1_en: Check your work for any error.
example2_en: Researchers should check their calculations carefully, as a minor error can significantly affect the final conclusions.
example2_zh: 研究人员应仔细核查计算过程，因为一个小错误就可能显著影响最终结论。
collocations: make an error｜犯错 ; human error｜人为失误 ; a margin of error｜误差范围 ; trial and error｜反复试验
tip_zh: error比mistake正式，常用于技术、计算或判断。

meanings_zh: v. 附上；贴上 | v. 赋予；认为具有
definition_en: to fasten or join | Consider something to have a particular value or importance
example1_en: Please attach your photo to the form.
example2_en: Many employers attach greater importance to practical experience than to academic qualifications when recruiting new staff.
example2_zh: 许多雇主招聘新员工时，更看重实际经验而非学历。
collocations: attach a file｜附上文件 ; attach something to something｜把某物固定到某物上 ; attach importance to｜重视
tip_zh: 常用attach A to B；邮件附件用attachment。

meanings_zh: v. 负担得起 | v. 提供；给予
definition_en: to have enough money or time for | to provide something useful or desirable
example1_en: We cannot afford to waste water.
example2_en: Without financial assistance, many students cannot afford to attend university despite having strong academic potential.
example2_zh: 如果没有经济援助，许多学生即使有很强的学术潜力，也无力负担大学费用。
collocations: can afford to do｜有能力负担做某事 ; cannot afford to lose｜承受不起失去 ; afford protection｜提供保护
tip_zh: 常用can afford sth或can afford to do，不接doing。

meanings_zh: adj. 主要的；重大的 | n. 主修专业；该专业学生 | v. 主修
definition_en: important; large | a main university subject, or a student studying that subject | to study a particular subject as your main university subject
example1_en: Traffic is a major problem.
example2_en: Access to affordable childcare remains a major concern for parents who wish to return to work.
example2_zh: 对于希望重返职场的父母而言，能否获得负担得起的托育服务仍是一个主要顾虑。
collocations: major problem｜重大问题 ; major role｜重要作用 ; major in biology｜主修生物学 ; major breakthrough｜重大突破
tip_zh: 动词主修用major in；主要用于美式英语。

meanings_zh: adj. 熟悉的 | adj. 熟知的；了解的
definition_en: well known | having knowledge or experience of something
example1_en: This song sounds familiar.
example2_en: Students who are familiar with digital tools may adapt more easily to online learning environments.
example2_zh: 熟悉数字工具的学生可能更容易适应在线学习环境。
collocations: familiar with｜熟悉…… ; familiar to｜为……所熟悉 ; a familiar face｜熟悉的面孔 ; look familiar｜看起来眼熟
tip_zh: 人熟悉事物用with；事物为人熟悉用to。

meanings_zh: v. 应得
definition_en: to be worthy of
example1_en: You deserve a rest after such hard work.
example1_zh: 这么辛苦之后你应得休息。
example2_en: Healthcare workers deserve greater recognition because their dedication contributes directly to the wellbeing of society.
example2_zh: 医护人员值得获得更多认可，因为他们的奉献直接促进了社会福祉。
collocations: deserve praise｜值得表扬 ; deserve attention｜值得关注 ; deserve to win｜理应获胜
tip_zh: 接名词或to do；不用deserve doing表示主动。

meanings_zh: adj. 精神的；心理的 | adj. 脑力的；在头脑中进行的
definition_en: of the mind | Using thought rather than physical action or written calculation.
example1_en: mental health matters as much as body health.
example1_zh: 心理健康与身体健康同样重要。
example2_en: Employers should give mental wellbeing the same priority as physical safety when designing workplace policies.
example2_zh: 雇主制定职场政策时，应将心理健康与人身安全放在同等重要的位置。
collocations: mental health｜心理健康 ; mental wellbeing｜心理幸福感 ; mental arithmetic｜心算 ; mental effort｜脑力付出
tip_zh: mental侧重心理或脑力；口语中形容人疯狂可能冒犯。

meanings_zh: v. 有益于 | v. 使受益；得益于 | n. 福利金；补助金
definition_en: to be good for | to help someone or receive help or an advantage | money provided by the government to people needing support
example1_en: Exercise can benefit both body and mind.
example2_en: Rural communities can benefit from improved internet access through greater opportunities for education and employment.
example2_zh: 更好的互联网接入能增加教育和就业机会，让农村社区受益。
collocations: health benefits｜健康益处 ; benefit from｜从……中受益 ; unemployment benefit｜失业救济金 ; mutual benefit｜互利
tip_zh: benefit sb指使某人受益；benefit from指得益于。

meanings_zh: n. 背景 | n. 背景情况 | n. 背景；后景
definition_en: past experience or setting | Information or events needed to understand a situation | The part of a scene behind the main subject
example1_en: Her family background shaped her views.
example1_zh: 她的家庭背景塑造了她的观点。
example2_en: Universities should provide equal opportunities for applicants from different social backgrounds, regardless of their family income.
example2_zh: 大学应为来自不同社会背景的申请者提供平等机会，不论其家庭收入如何。
collocations: a professional background｜职业背景 ; background information｜背景资料 ; in the background｜在背景中 ; a disadvantaged background｜弱势家庭背景
tip_zh: 经历领域用background in；背景中用in the background。

meanings_zh: adj. 直接的 | v. 指导；指挥；导演 | v. 指路；将……指向
definition_en: straight; clear | To guide or control an activity, performance, or group. | To show the way or aim something towards a place.
example1_en: Take the direct route home.
example2_en: Improved public transport can have a direct impact on employment by connecting residents with more job opportunities.
example2_zh: 改善公共交通能让居民获得更多就业机会，从而对就业产生直接影响。
collocations: direct contact｜直接接触 ; a direct flight｜直达航班 ; direct a film｜导演电影 ; direct attention to｜将注意力转向
tip_zh: direct可作形容词或动词；常见读音也有/daɪˈrekt/。

meanings_zh: v. 使困惑 | v. 混淆；认错
definition_en: to make unclear or mixed up | To wrongly think one person or thing is another.
example1_en: Too many choices may confuse buyers.
example1_zh: 选择太多可能让买家困惑。
example2_en: Public health messages can confuse audiences when experts use technical language without explaining its meaning.
example2_zh: 专家使用术语却不解释其含义时，公共卫生信息可能会让受众感到困惑。
collocations: confuse A with B｜把A与B混淆 ; confuse the issue｜把问题弄复杂 ; easily confused｜容易混淆的
tip_zh: confused形容人感到困惑；confusing形容事物令人困惑。

meanings_zh: adj. 好奇的 | adj. 奇怪的；不寻常的
definition_en: wanting to know more | Unusual or strange in a way that attracts attention.
example1_en: Children are curious about nature.
example2_en: Teachers can encourage curious students to explore scientific questions through practical experiments rather than memorisation alone.
example2_zh: 教师可以鼓励求知欲强的学生通过动手实验探索科学问题，而不只是死记硬背。
collocations: curious about｜对……好奇 ; curious to know｜很想知道 ; a curious mixture｜奇特的混合物
tip_zh: be curious about表示“对……好奇”。

meanings_zh: adj. 杰出的；明亮的 | adj. 才华出众的；聪颖的 | adj. 明亮的；灿烂的
definition_en: very clever or bright | Exceptionally intelligent or skilled. | Shining brightly or having a strong, vivid colour.
example1_en: She had a brilliant idea.
example2_en: Brilliant teachers can inspire students to explore difficult subjects with confidence and genuine curiosity.
example2_zh: 出色的教师能激励学生带着信心和真正的好奇心探索难学的科目。
collocations: brilliant idea｜绝妙的主意 ; brilliant scientist｜杰出的科学家 ; brilliant sunshine｜灿烂的阳光
tip_zh: 英式口语中常用 brilliant 表示“太棒了”。

meanings_zh: adj. 每日的
definition_en: happening every day
example1_en: Exercise is part of her daily routine.
example1_zh: 锻炼是她每日例行的一部分。

meanings_zh: v. 道歉
definition_en: to say sorry
example1_en: You should apologize for being late.
example2_en: Companies should apologize promptly for service failures and explain what steps they will take to prevent further problems.
example2_zh: 企业应及时为服务失误道歉，并说明将采取哪些措施来防止问题再次发生。
collocations: apologize to someone｜向某人道歉 ; apologize for doing something｜为做某事道歉 ; apologize sincerely｜真诚道歉
tip_zh: 向人道歉用to，为事情道歉用for；英式也写apologise。

meanings_zh: adj. 自信的 | adj. 确信的；有把握的
definition_en: sure of yourself | certain that something is true or will happen
example1_en: Speak in a confident voice.
example2_en: Students become more confident when teachers provide constructive feedback and opportunities to practise new skills.
example2_zh: 当教师提供建设性反馈和练习新技能的机会时，学生会变得更自信。
collocations: feel confident｜感到自信 ; confident about the future｜对未来有信心 ; confident that｜确信
tip_zh: confident是形容词；confidence是名词。

meanings_zh: adj. 可能的
definition_en: probable
example1_en: Rain is likely today.

meanings_zh: n. 努力 | n. 尝试；有组织的行动
definition_en: hard work | an attempt or organised activity intended to achieve a goal
example1_en: Success needs continuous effort.
example2_en: Reducing household waste requires a joint effort from consumers, manufacturers and local authorities to change everyday practices.
example2_zh: 减少家庭垃圾需要消费者、制造商和地方政府共同努力，改变日常做法。
collocations: make an effort｜作出努力 ; put effort into｜投入精力于 ; a joint effort｜共同努力 ; considerable effort｜相当大的努力
tip_zh: 表示精力时不可数；表示一次尝试时可数。

meanings_zh: n. 信念；信仰
definition_en: something accepted as true
example1_en: Strong belief can give people hope.
example1_zh: 坚定的信念能给人希望。
example2_en: The belief that education improves social mobility influences government spending priorities in many countries.
example2_zh: 教育能促进社会流动的这一信念影响着许多国家的政府支出重点。
collocations: belief in someone｜对某人的信任 ; religious beliefs｜宗教信仰 ; a widely held belief｜普遍持有的看法 ; contrary to popular belief｜与普遍看法相反
tip_zh: belief in表示信任或信仰；belief that后接具体看法。

meanings_zh: v. 说服
definition_en: to make someone believe
example1_en: She tried to convince him to stay.
example2_en: Governments must convince residents that improved public transport offers a practical alternative to private cars.
example2_zh: 政府必须让居民相信，改善后的公共交通能够切实替代私家车出行。
collocations: convince someone of something｜使某人相信某事 ; convince someone that｜使某人确信 ; convince someone to do something｜说服某人做某事
tip_zh: convince sb of sth表示使某人相信某事。

meanings_zh: v. 要求 | n. 坚决要求 | v. 强烈要求；需要
definition_en: to ask for firmly | a strong request that someone expects to be obeyed | to insist on receiving something or require something essential
example1_en: Workers demand better pay and safety.
example1_zh: 工人们要求更好的薪酬和安全。
example2_en: Growing demand for affordable housing has encouraged local authorities to convert unused office buildings into residential accommodation.
example2_zh: 对可负担住房不断增长的需求促使地方政府将闲置办公楼改建为住宅。
collocations: demand for housing｜住房需求 ; meet demand｜满足需求 ; in high demand｜需求旺盛 ; demand an explanation｜要求解释
tip_zh: 要求做某事用demand to do，不用demand sb to do。

meanings_zh: v. 承认；准许进入 | v. 准许进入；接收
definition_en: to say something is true; to allow in | to allow someone to enter or join a place or institution
example1_en: He had to admit that he was wrong.
example1_zh: 他不得不承认自己错了。
example2_en: Governments should admit when policies have failed and use reliable evidence to develop more effective alternatives.
example2_zh: 政府应承认政策失败，并依据可靠证据制定更有效的替代方案。
collocations: admit a mistake｜承认错误 ; admit doing something｜承认做过某事 ; admit that｜承认…… ; be admitted to hospital｜被收治入院
tip_zh: 用admit doing，不用admit to do；过去式双写t。

meanings_zh: v. 宣布
definition_en: to make known publicly
example1_en: The teacher will announce the exam date tomorrow.
example1_zh: 老师明天会宣布考试日期。
example2_en: Local authorities should announce major policy changes early so residents have enough time to prepare.
example2_zh: 地方政府应尽早公布重大政策调整，让居民有充足的准备时间。
collocations: announce plans｜宣布计划 ; announce a decision｜宣布决定 ; announce the results｜公布结果
tip_zh: 用announce sth或announce that，不用announce sb sth。

meanings_zh: v. 呼吸
definition_en: to take air in and out
example1_en: It is hard to breathe in heavy smoke.
example2_en: People living near busy roads often breathe polluted air, which can increase their risk of respiratory illness.
example2_zh: 住在繁忙道路附近的人经常吸入受污染的空气，这可能增加他们患呼吸系统疾病的风险。
collocations: breathe deeply｜深呼吸 ; breathe in｜吸气 ; breathe out｜呼气 ; breathe fresh air｜呼吸新鲜空气
tip_zh: breathe是动词，末音/ð/；breath是名词，末音/θ/。

meanings_zh: adj. 诚实的 | adj. 坦率的；真诚的
definition_en: truthful | Expressing what you really think or feel.
example1_en: Be honest about your mistakes.
example2_en: Honest communication between teachers and parents can help schools address students' difficulties before they become serious.
example2_zh: 教师与家长之间坦诚的沟通能帮助学校在学生的问题变得严重之前加以解决。
collocations: an honest person｜诚实的人 ; an honest answer｜坦率的回答 ; to be honest｜说实话
tip_zh: h不发音，因此说an honest person。

meanings_zh: v. 损害；毁坏 | v. 损坏；损害
definition_en: to harm | Harm something or make it less effective.
example1_en: Floods can damage houses and roads.
example1_zh: 洪水会毁坏房屋和道路。
example2_en: Uncontrolled tourism can damage fragile ecosystems and reduce the quality of life for local residents.
example2_zh: 不受控制的旅游活动可能破坏脆弱的生态系统，并降低当地居民的生活质量。
collocations: cause damage｜造成损害 ; damage to property｜财产损坏 ; environmental damage｜环境破坏 ; damage someone's reputation｜损害某人的声誉
tip_zh: 损害用不可数damage；damages指法律赔偿金。

meanings_zh: adj. 感激的
definition_en: thankful
example1_en: I am grateful for your help.
example2_en: Many students are grateful for scholarships that allow them to continue their education despite financial difficulties.
example2_zh: 许多学生感谢奖学金让他们即使经济困难也能继续学业。
collocations: grateful to someone｜感激某人 ; grateful for something｜感谢某事 ; deeply grateful｜深表感激
tip_zh: be grateful to某人 for某事；注意不是greatful。

meanings_zh: adj. 简短的 | v. 向……介绍情况 | n. 任务说明；工作要求
definition_en: short in time or words | To give someone essential information or instructions. | Instructions explaining what a task should achieve.
example1_en: Give a brief summary.
example2_en: Teachers should brief students on safety procedures before allowing them to conduct experiments independently.
example2_zh: 教师应先向学生介绍安全操作规程，再允许他们独立进行实验。
collocations: a brief summary｜简要总结 ; a brief pause｜短暂停顿 ; brief someone on｜向某人介绍……的情况 ; a design brief｜设计任务说明
tip_zh: brief指时间短或内容简洁，本身不表示草率。

meanings_zh: v. 得出结论；结束
definition_en: to decide after thinking; to end
example1_en: We can conclude that practice helps.
example1_zh: 我们可以得出结论：练习有帮助。

meanings_zh: v. 影响 | v. 使感动；使悲伤
definition_en: to have an influence on | to cause someone to feel a strong emotion
example1_en: Noise can affect your ability to sleep.
example1_zh: 噪音会影响你的睡眠能力。
example2_en: Rising food prices disproportionately affect poorer households, which spend a larger share of their income on essentials.
example2_zh: 食品价格上涨对较贫困家庭的影响尤为严重，因为必需品支出占其收入的比例更大。
collocations: affect health｜影响健康 ; adversely affect｜产生不利影响 ; deeply affect someone｜深深触动某人 ; affect performance｜影响表现
tip_zh: 表示“影响”时affect是动词，effect通常是名词。

meanings_zh: n. 优势；有利条件 | n. 好处；益处
definition_en: something that helps you | A useful or positive feature of something.
example1_en: Speaking two languages is an advantage.
example1_zh: 会说两种语言是一种优势。
example2_en: One major advantage of public transport is its ability to reduce traffic congestion in urban areas.
example2_zh: 公共交通的一大好处是能够缓解城市地区的交通拥堵。
collocations: competitive advantage｜竞争优势 ; have an advantage over｜比……有优势 ; take advantage of｜利用；占……便宜 ; a major advantage｜一大优势
tip_zh: take advantage of可指利用机会，也可指占人便宜。

meanings_zh: v. 收费；充电；指控 | n. 费用；收费 | v. 给……充电
definition_en: to ask for money; to accuse | An amount of money requested for goods or services. | Put electrical energy into a battery or device.
example1_en: Hotels often charge extra for breakfast.
example1_zh: 酒店常对早餐额外收费。
example2_en: Museums that charge admission fees should offer discounts to ensure that students can still access cultural resources.
example2_zh: 收取门票的博物馆应提供优惠，以确保学生仍能享用文化资源。
collocations: charge a fee｜收取费用 ; free of charge｜免费 ; charge a battery｜给电池充电 ; in charge of｜负责；掌管
tip_zh: 向某人收取某项费用：charge someone for something。

meanings_zh: n. 态度
definition_en: a way of thinking or feeling
example1_en: A positive attitude helps in hard times.
example1_zh: 积极态度有助于渡过难关。
example2_en: Schools can encourage a positive attitude towards learning by giving students constructive feedback rather than constant criticism.
example2_zh: 学校可以给予学生建设性的反馈，而非不断批评，以培养积极的学习态度。
collocations: positive attitude｜积极的态度 ; attitude towards｜对……的态度 ; change of attitude｜态度的转变 ; public attitudes｜公众态度
tip_zh: 对某事的态度常用attitude to或towards。

meanings_zh: n. 影响；效果 | v. 实现；使发生
definition_en: a result | To bring about a change or result.
example1_en: Sleep has a strong effect on mood.
example1_zh: 睡眠对情绪有强烈影响。
example2_en: Higher parking charges may have little effect on traffic unless reliable public transport is also available.
example2_zh: 如果没有可靠的公共交通，提高停车费对交通状况的影响可能很小。
collocations: have an effect on｜对……有影响 ; side effect｜副作用 ; take effect｜生效；起作用 ; effect change｜促成变革
tip_zh: effect常作名词；affect常作动词，意为影响。

meanings_zh: v. 申请；应用 | v. 应用；适用 | v. 涂；敷
definition_en: to ask formally; to use | To use something practically, or be relevant to a situation | To spread a substance onto a surface
example1_en: She will apply for a scholarship.
example2_en: Universities should encourage students from disadvantaged backgrounds to apply for scholarships that cover tuition and living expenses.
example2_zh: 大学应鼓励家庭条件困难的学生申请涵盖学费和生活费的奖学金。
collocations: apply for a job｜申请工作 ; apply to a university｜向大学提出申请 ; apply knowledge｜应用知识 ; apply sunscreen｜涂防晒霜
tip_zh: apply for接申请事项；apply to接机构或适用对象。

meanings_zh: adj. 立即的 | adj. 速溶的；即食的 | n. 瞬间；片刻
definition_en: happening at once | prepared very quickly, usually by adding hot water | an extremely short period of time
example1_en: She got an instant reply.
example2_en: Digital platforms provide instant access to educational resources, although reliable internet connections remain essential.
example2_zh: 数字平台让人们即时获取教育资源，但稳定的网络连接仍然必不可少。
collocations: instant access｜即时获取 ; instant results｜即时结果 ; instant coffee｜速溶咖啡 ; in an instant｜转眼间
tip_zh: instant作形容词表示即时的；in an instant表示转眼间。

meanings_zh: n. 结论；结尾 | n. 结尾；结束
definition_en: a final decision or end | the final part or ending of something
example1_en: The conclusion of the report is clear.
example2_en: Researchers should consider alternative explanations before drawing a conclusion from a relatively small sample.
example2_zh: 研究人员根据较小的样本得出结论之前，应考虑其他可能的解释。
collocations: reach a conclusion｜得出结论 ; draw a conclusion｜作出推断 ; jump to conclusions｜贸然下结论 ; in conclusion｜总而言之
tip_zh: “得出结论”用reach或draw a conclusion，不用make。

meanings_zh: n. 目标；目的 | v. 力求；旨在 | v. 瞄准；对准
definition_en: a purpose or goal | to intend or try to achieve something | to point something towards a particular target
example1_en: Our aim is to finish on time.
example1_zh: 我们的目标是按时完成。
example2_en: The programme aims to reduce youth unemployment by providing practical training and opportunities to gain workplace experience.
example2_zh: 该项目旨在通过提供实践培训和获取职场经验的机会，降低青年失业率。
collocations: the main aim｜主要目标 ; aim to do something｜力求做某事 ; with the aim of｜以……为目的 ; aim at a target｜瞄准目标
tip_zh: aim to do表打算做；aim at doing表力求实现。

meanings_zh: adj. 复杂的 | n. 综合建筑群
definition_en: having many parts | A group of buildings used for related activities.
example1_en: The problem is more complex than it looks.
example2_en: Urban poverty is a complex issue that requires cooperation between governments, businesses and local communities.
example2_zh: 城市贫困是一个复杂问题，需要政府、企业和当地社区共同合作。
collocations: complex issue｜复杂问题 ; complex system｜复杂系统 ; sports complex｜综合体育场馆
tip_zh: 作形容词指复杂；作名词可指综合建筑群。

meanings_zh: n. 解释 | n. 原因；解释理由
definition_en: words that make something clear | a reason given for why something happened
example1_en: Her explanation helped us understand.
example1_zh: 她的解释帮助我们理解。
example2_en: One possible explanation for declining car ownership is the growing availability of reliable public transport.
example2_zh: 汽车拥有率下降的一个可能原因，是可靠的公共交通越来越普及。
collocations: clear explanation｜清楚的解释 ; give an explanation｜作出解释 ; explanation for｜对……的原因解释 ; explanation of｜对……的说明
tip_zh: explanation of多说明内容，for多解释原因。

meanings_zh: adj. 整个的
definition_en: whole
example1_en: The entire class passed the test.
example1_zh: 整个班级都通过了考试。

meanings_zh: v. 竞争 | v. 参加比赛
definition_en: to try to win against others | Take part in a sporting event or other contest.
example1_en: Many teams compete for the prize.
example1_zh: 许多队伍竞争这个奖项。
example2_en: Small businesses often struggle to compete with larger companies that can offer lower prices.
example2_zh: 小企业往往难以与能够提供更低价格的大公司竞争。
collocations: compete with｜与……竞争 ; compete for｜争夺 ; compete in a tournament｜参加锦标赛
tip_zh: compete with/against对手；for奖项；in赛事。

meanings_zh: adj. 独立的 | adj. 不受控制的；独立的 | adj. 无关联的；互不影响的
definition_en: not needing others' control | not controlled by another person, organisation, or country | not connected with or affected by something else
example1_en: She became more independent at college.
example2_en: Independent research can help governments assess whether new environmental policies are achieving their intended goals.
example2_zh: 独立研究可以帮助政府评估新的环境政策是否正在实现预期目标。
collocations: financially independent｜经济独立的 ; independent research｜独立研究 ; independent of｜不依赖；不受影响 ; independent judgement｜独立判断
tip_zh: 常搭配of：independent of意为不依赖或不受影响。

meanings_zh: n. 焦点；重点 | n. 重点；关注中心 | n. 清晰度；焦点
definition_en: the center of attention | the main subject receiving attention or effort | image sharpness, or the point where light rays meet
example1_en: Keep your focus on the task.
example1_zh: 把注意力集中在任务上。
example2_en: Governments should focus on affordable public transport to reduce congestion and improve access to employment.
example2_zh: 政府应重点发展价格合理的公共交通，以缓解拥堵并改善就业机会的可达性。
collocations: focus on｜集中于 ; the main focus｜主要关注点 ; in focus｜影像清晰 ; out of focus｜影像模糊
tip_zh: focus on后接名词或动名词；不要说focus in。

meanings_zh: adj. 频繁的 | v. 常去；常到访
definition_en: happening often | Visit a particular place regularly
example1_en: frequent rain delayed the flight.
example1_zh: 频繁的降雨延误了航班。
example2_en: Frequent changes in education policy can make it difficult for teachers to plan effective lessons.
example2_zh: 教育政策频繁变化，可能使教师难以规划有效的课堂教学。
collocations: frequent visits｜频繁到访 ; frequent delays｜频繁延误 ; a frequent visitor｜常客 ; frequent changes｜频繁变化
tip_zh: 形容词重音在首音节；动词重音在第二音节。

meanings_zh: adj. 意识到的
definition_en: knowing about something
example1_en: Be aware of the risks.

meanings_zh: v. 结合；联合 | n. 联合收割机
definition_en: to join together | A farm machine that harvests grain and separates the seeds.
example1_en: Good teachers combine hard work with creativity.
example1_zh: 好老师把努力与创造力结合起来。
example2_en: Cities can combine improved public transport with safer cycling routes to reduce dependence on private cars.
example2_zh: 城市可以将公共交通改善与更安全的骑行路线建设相结合，减少对私家车的依赖。
collocations: combine A with B｜把A与B结合 ; combine efforts｜合力 ; combine theory and practice｜理论与实践相结合
tip_zh: 动词重音在后；收割机名词读/ˈkɒmbaɪn/。

meanings_zh: v. 吸收；使全神贯注
definition_en: to take in; to hold one's attention
example1_en: Plants absorb water through their roots.
example1_zh: 植物通过根部吸收水分。

meanings_zh: n. 外貌；出现 | n. 出现；露面
definition_en: how someone looks; the act of showing up | an occasion when someone or something becomes visible or present
example1_en: First appearance can be misleading.
example1_zh: 第一印象可能具有误导性。
example2_en: Employers should assess candidates on their skills and experience rather than judging them by their appearance.
example2_zh: 雇主应根据应聘者的技能和经验进行评估，而不是以貌取人。
collocations: physical appearance｜外貌 ; make an appearance｜露面 ; outward appearance｜外表 ; improve the appearance of｜改善……的外观
tip_zh: 外貌与露面都可用appearance；露面常用make an appearance。

meanings_zh: n. 基础；根据 | n. 方式；频率
definition_en: the main support or reason | The arrangement or frequency according to which something happens.
example1_en: Trust is the basis of friendship.
example2_en: Reliable evidence should provide the basis for government decisions about public health and environmental protection.
example2_zh: 可靠的证据应成为政府作出公共卫生和环境保护决策的依据。
collocations: on a daily basis｜每天 ; on the basis of｜根据 ; form the basis of｜构成……的基础 ; a sound basis｜坚实的基础
tip_zh: 复数为bases；on a daily basis意为每天。

meanings_zh: n. 文化 | n. 文化艺术活动 | n. 培养物
definition_en: shared customs and arts | activities involving art, music, literature and other creative work | cells or microorganisms grown under controlled conditions
example1_en: Food is part of local culture.
example1_zh: 食物是当地文化的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving local culture can strengthen community identity while allowing residents to benefit from international exchange.
example2_zh: 保护本土文化可以增强社区认同，同时让居民受益于国际交流。
collocations: local culture｜本土文化 ; cultural exchange｜文化交流 ; popular culture｜流行文化 ; bacterial culture｜细菌培养物
tip_zh: 泛指文化通常不可数；不同文化可用cultures。

meanings_zh: adj. 较年幼的；初级的 | adj. 青少年的；年少的 | n. 低年级学生；较年幼者
definition_en: younger or lower in rank | Intended for younger people or involving them | A younger person, or a student below the final year
example1_en: He is a junior member of the team.
example2_en: Companies should provide junior employees with structured training and regular opportunities to learn from experienced colleagues.
example2_zh: 公司应为初级员工提供系统培训，并定期安排他们向经验丰富的同事学习。
collocations: junior staff｜初级员工 ; junior position｜初级职位 ; junior championship｜青少年锦标赛
tip_zh: 职位或年龄比较用junior to，不用junior than。

meanings_zh: n. 平均数；一般水平 | n. 平均数；平均水平 | v. 平均为
definition_en: the usual level or mean | A value calculated by dividing a total by the item count. | Have a particular amount as the usual or calculated middle value.
example1_en: His scores are above the average.
example1_zh: 他的分数高于平均水平。
example2_en: Average household spending on energy may fall as better insulation reduces the need for heating.
example2_zh: 随着更好的隔热措施减少供暖需求，家庭能源支出的平均水平可能下降。
collocations: on average｜平均而言 ; above average｜高于平均水平 ; average income｜平均收入 ; average temperature｜平均气温
tip_zh: on average表示“平均而言”，不用in average。

meanings_zh: v. 考虑；认为 | v. 认为；视为 | v. 顾及；考虑到
definition_en: to think about carefully | to have a particular opinion about someone or something | to take someone or something into account
example1_en: Please consider my advice before deciding.
example1_zh: 做决定前请考虑我的建议。
example2_en: Governments should consider the long-term environmental costs before approving major construction projects in sensitive coastal areas.
example2_zh: 政府在批准生态敏感沿海地区的大型建设项目之前，应考虑其长期环境成本。
collocations: consider doing something｜考虑做某事 ; consider the consequences｜考虑后果 ; consider all options｜考虑所有选择 ; be considered essential｜被认为必不可少
tip_zh: “考虑做”用consider doing，不用consider to do。

meanings_zh: n. 气候 | n. 社会环境；风气；氛围
definition_en: usual weather of a place | The general attitudes and conditions within a society or organisation.
example1_en: The climate here is warm and wet.
example2_en: A changing climate may force farmers to grow different crops and adopt more efficient irrigation methods.
example2_zh: 气候变化可能迫使农民改种其他作物，并采用更高效的灌溉方法。
collocations: climate change｜气候变化 ; mild climate｜温和的气候 ; political climate｜政治环境
tip_zh: climate指长期气候，weather指具体天气。

meanings_zh: n. 勇气
definition_en: bravery
example1_en: It takes courage to speak in public.
example2_en: Young people need courage to challenge unfair practices, especially when their opinions differ from those of others.
example2_zh: 年轻人需要勇气来质疑不公平的做法，尤其是在自己的观点与他人不同时。
collocations: have the courage to do something｜有勇气做某事 ; show courage｜表现出勇气 ; take courage｜鼓起勇气
tip_zh: 通常不可数；做某事的勇气用courage to do。

meanings_zh: v. 防守；辩护 | v. 辩护；捍卫 | v. 防守
definition_en: to protect from attack | to give reasons supporting someone or something being criticised | to prevent opponents from scoring in a sport
example1_en: Soldiers defend the city from danger.
example1_zh: 士兵们保卫城市免受危险。
example2_en: Governments should defend citizens' rights while ensuring that public safety measures remain fair and proportionate.
example2_zh: 政府应捍卫公民权利，同时确保公共安全措施公平且适度。
collocations: defend against attack｜抵御攻击 ; defend human rights｜捍卫人权 ; defend a decision｜为某项决定辩护 ; defend a title｜卫冕
tip_zh: defend ... against/from ...表示保护……免受……。

meanings_zh: n. 观众；听众 | n. 读者群；受众
definition_en: people watching or listening | People who read or receive particular content
example1_en: The audience clapped after the show.
example2_en: Online platforms enable museums to reach a wider audience, including people who cannot visit their collections in person.
example2_zh: 网络平台使博物馆能够接触更广泛的受众，包括无法亲自参观馆藏的人。
collocations: a large audience｜众多观众 ; a target audience｜目标受众 ; reach a wider audience｜触达更广泛的受众 ; audience participation｜观众参与
tip_zh: 观众多用large audience，不用many audiences。

meanings_zh: v. 计算
definition_en: to work out a number
example1_en: Can you calculate the total cost?

meanings_zh: n. 灾难 | n. 彻底的失败；糟糕的事
definition_en: a sudden serious event causing harm | Something that goes extremely badly or fails completely.
example1_en: An earthquake is a natural disaster.
example2_en: Effective early warning systems can reduce the damage caused by natural disasters and help communities recover more quickly.
example2_zh: 有效的预警系统可以减少自然灾害造成的损失，并帮助社区更快恢复。
collocations: natural disaster｜自然灾害 ; disaster relief｜灾害救援 ; avert disaster｜避免灾难 ; a complete disaster｜彻底的失败
tip_zh: 也可夸张形容失败：The party was a disaster。

meanings_zh: v. 钦佩；羡慕 | v. 欣赏；赞赏
definition_en: to respect or look up to someone | To look at something with pleasure because it is attractive
example1_en: I admire her courage in difficult times.
example1_zh: 我钦佩她在困难时期的勇气。
example2_en: People often admire successful athletes for their determination, but consistent training is equally important.
example2_zh: 人们常因成功运动员的毅力而钦佩他们，但坚持训练同样重要。
collocations: admire someone for something｜因某事钦佩某人 ; greatly admire｜十分钦佩 ; admire the view｜欣赏风景
tip_zh: admire sb for sth：因某事钦佩某人。

meanings_zh: n. 条件；状况 | n. 条件；环境 | n. 疾病；健康问题
definition_en: a state or requirement | A requirement, or circumstances affecting life or activity | A medical problem affecting someone's health
example1_en: The road is in poor condition.
example2_en: Improving working conditions can increase employee satisfaction and reduce the number of people leaving their jobs.
example2_zh: 改善工作条件可以提高员工满意度，并减少离职人数。
collocations: in good condition｜状况良好 ; working conditions｜工作条件 ; on condition that｜条件是 ; medical condition｜疾病；健康问题
tip_zh: 表状态通常不可数；表工作、生活环境常用复数。

meanings_zh: adj. 合法的；法律的 | adj. 合法的；法律允许的
definition_en: allowed by law | Allowed by the law
example1_en: Is this action legal?
example2_en: Access to affordable legal services is essential for ensuring that disadvantaged citizens can defend their rights.
example2_zh: 让人们获得负担得起的法律服务，对保障弱势公民维护自身权利至关重要。
collocations: legal advice｜法律意见 ; legal action｜法律诉讼 ; legal rights｜法定权利 ; perfectly legal｜完全合法
tip_zh: legal可指“法律相关的”，不一定指“合法的”。

meanings_zh: n. 专家 | adj. 专业的；熟练的
definition_en: a person with special skill | Having or showing great knowledge or skill.
example1_en: Ask an expert for advice.
example2_en: Schools should seek expert advice before introducing new technology into classrooms to support student learning.
example2_zh: 学校在将新技术引入课堂以辅助学生学习之前，应征求专家意见。
collocations: an expert on｜某方面的专家 ; expert advice｜专家建议 ; medical expert｜医学专家
tip_zh: expert on/in表示某领域的专家。

meanings_zh: v. 向…挑战 | v. 质疑；提出异议 | v. 向…挑战；考验
definition_en: to invite someone to compete or try hard | Question whether something is true, fair, or acceptable. | Invite someone to compete or test their abilities.
example1_en: This puzzle will challenge your mind.
example1_zh: 这道谜题会挑战你的思维。
example2_en: Providing affordable housing remains a major challenge for cities experiencing rapid population growth and rising land prices.
example2_zh: 对于人口快速增长、地价不断上涨的城市而言，提供可负担住房仍是一项重大挑战。
collocations: face a challenge｜面临挑战 ; meet a challenge｜成功应对挑战 ; challenge an assumption｜质疑假设 ; challenge someone to a contest｜向某人发起比赛挑战
tip_zh: challenge作动词可直接接观点，表示质疑。

meanings_zh: n. 困难 | n. 难题；困境
definition_en: a problem | A problem that makes progress or success harder.
example1_en: She overcame great difficulty to succeed.
example1_zh: 她克服巨大困难获得成功。
example2_en: Students with limited internet access may have difficulty completing assignments that require extensive online research.
example2_zh: 网络使用受限的学生可能难以完成需要大量网上研究的作业。
collocations: have difficulty doing something｜做某事有困难 ; overcome difficulties｜克服困难 ; financial difficulties｜经济困难 ; with difficulty｜费力地
tip_zh: 用have difficulty doing，不用difficulty to do。

meanings_zh: v. 包含 | v. 控制；遏制
definition_en: to have inside | to prevent something from spreading or becoming stronger
example1_en: This box may contain old letters.
example1_zh: 这个盒子里可能装有旧信。
example2_en: Processed foods often contain large amounts of salt, which can contribute to serious health problems.
example2_zh: 加工食品往往含有大量盐分，可能导致严重的健康问题。
collocations: contain ingredients｜含有成分 ; contain the spread｜遏制蔓延 ; contain costs｜控制成本 ; contain your excitement｜抑制兴奋
tip_zh: 及物动词，直接接宾语；表示“含有”时通常不用进行时。

meanings_zh: v. 递送；发表 | v. 发表；讲授 | v. 兑现；实现
definition_en: to take to a place; to give a speech | to give a speech, lecture, or presentation | to produce the results or benefits that were promised
example1_en: The post office will deliver the package.
example2_en: Public transport projects must deliver clear benefits to local residents if they are to justify substantial investment.
example2_zh: 公共交通项目必须为当地居民带来明确的益处，才能证明大规模投资是合理的。
collocations: deliver a parcel｜递送包裹 ; deliver a speech｜发表演讲 ; deliver results｜取得成效 ; deliver on a promise｜兑现承诺
tip_zh: 递送用deliver sth to sb；兑现承诺可用deliver on。

meanings_zh: n. 成就 | n. 实现；达成
definition_en: something successfully done | The successful completion of a goal through effort.
example1_en: Winning the prize was a great achievement.
example2_en: Schools should recognise creative achievements alongside examination results to encourage a wider range of student abilities.
example2_zh: 学校应在重视考试成绩的同时认可创造性成果，以鼓励学生发展多方面的能力。
collocations: a major achievement｜重大成就 ; a sense of achievement｜成就感 ; academic achievement｜学业成绩 ; the achievement of goals｜目标的实现
tip_zh: 具体成就可数；表示目标的实现时通常不可数。

meanings_zh: v. 确认 | v. 确认安排；正式批准
definition_en: to make sure something is true | To make an arrangement certain or give it official approval.
example1_en: Please confirm your email address.
example1_zh: 请确认你的电子邮箱地址。
example2_en: Further research is needed to confirm whether smaller classes consistently improve learning outcomes in primary schools.
example2_zh: 还需要进一步研究，以证实小学小班教学是否能持续改善学习效果。
collocations: confirm a booking｜确认预订 ; confirm that｜证实…… ; confirm a diagnosis｜确诊 ; confirm receipt｜确认收到
tip_zh: 可接名词或that从句；不要用confirm to do。

meanings_zh: n. 申请；应用 | n. 应用；运用 | n. 应用程序
definition_en: a formal request; a use | the practical use of knowledge, skills, or methods | a computer program designed to perform particular tasks
example1_en: Send your application before Friday.
example2_en: Simplifying the application process could encourage more students from disadvantaged backgrounds to apply for university scholarships.
example2_zh: 简化申请流程可能鼓励更多来自弱势家庭的学生申请大学奖学金。
collocations: submit an application｜提交申请 ; application form｜申请表 ; practical application｜实际应用 ; software application｜软件应用程序
tip_zh: 申请某物用application for，向机构申请用to。

meanings_zh: n. 失败 | n. 故障；衰竭 | n. 未做；未履行
definition_en: lack of success | a situation in which a machine or organ stops working | not doing something that is expected or required
example1_en: failure can teach useful lessons.
example1_zh: 失败能教会有用的功课。
example2_en: Schools should treat failure as an opportunity for learning rather than as evidence of a student's limited ability.
example2_zh: 学校应将失败视为学习的机会，而不是学生能力有限的证明。
collocations: end in failure｜以失败告终 ; power failure｜停电 ; heart failure｜心力衰竭 ; failure to comply｜未遵守
tip_zh: 泛指失败通常不可数；a failure可指失败的事物。

meanings_zh: v. 吸引 | v. 吸引靠近
definition_en: to draw interest | Pull something closer through a physical force
example1_en: Bright colors attract many insects.
example1_zh: 鲜艳的颜色吸引许多昆虫。
example2_en: Cities that invest in reliable public transport are more likely to attract businesses and skilled workers.
example2_zh: 投资建设可靠公共交通的城市更有可能吸引企业和技术人才。
collocations: attract attention｜吸引注意 ; attract tourists｜吸引游客 ; attract investment｜吸引投资 ; attract customers｜吸引顾客
tip_zh: attract是及物动词，直接接人或事物作宾语。

meanings_zh: v. 打扰；烦恼 | v. 费心；花工夫 | n. 麻烦；烦扰
definition_en: to annoy or trouble | to make the effort to do something | trouble or effort that causes inconvenience
example1_en: Sorry to bother you so late.
example2_en: Constant notifications can bother students during lessons and reduce their ability to concentrate on complex tasks.
example2_zh: 持续不断的通知会在课堂上干扰学生，降低他们专注于复杂任务的能力。
collocations: bother someone with something｜拿某事打扰某人 ; bother to do something｜费心做某事 ; cannot be bothered｜懒得费事 ; a lot of bother｜很多麻烦
tip_zh: bother to do常用于否定或疑问，表示费心做。

meanings_zh: v. 不同；相异 | v. 意见不合
definition_en: to be unlike | To have a different opinion from another person.
example1_en: Opinions may differ among friends.
example1_zh: 朋友之间意见可能不同。
example2_en: Educational priorities differ between countries because economic conditions and cultural expectations shape national policies.
example2_zh: 各国的教育重点有所不同，因为经济条件和文化期待会影响国家政策。
collocations: differ from｜与……不同 ; differ in size｜大小不同 ; differ widely｜差异很大 ; differ with someone｜与某人意见不同
tip_zh: from引出比较对象，in引出差异方面。

meanings_zh: adj. 一般的；总体的 | adj. 大致的；非具体的 | n. 将军
definition_en: not detailed; overall | describing main points rather than particular details | an officer with a very high rank in the army
example1_en: In general, people prefer weekends.
example1_zh: 一般来说，人们更喜欢周末。
example2_en: Although the general standard of education has improved, significant differences remain between urban and rural schools.
example2_zh: 尽管教育总体水平已有提高，城乡学校之间仍存在显著差异。
collocations: in general｜一般来说 ; general public｜公众 ; general knowledge｜常识 ; general overview｜总体概述
tip_zh: in general意为“一般来说”，常用于概括。

meanings_zh: v. 责备 | n. 责任；责备
definition_en: to say someone is responsible for a fault | Responsibility for something bad that has happened.
example1_en: Don't blame others for your mistakes.
example1_zh: 不要把自己的错误归咎于别人。
example2_en: It is unfair to blame individuals alone for environmental problems caused partly by industrial activity.
example2_zh: 环境问题部分由工业活动造成，仅归咎于个人并不公平。
collocations: blame someone for something｜因某事责怪某人 ; blame something on someone｜把某事归咎于某人 ; take the blame｜承担责任 ; be to blame｜应负责任
tip_zh: 人作宾语用blame sb for；事作宾语用blame sth on。

meanings_zh: n. 公民 | n. 市民；居民
definition_en: a member of a country | A person who lives in a particular town or city.
example1_en: Every citizen has rights and duties.
example1_zh: 每个公民都有权利与义务。
example2_en: Every citizen should have access to reliable public services, regardless of income or place of residence.
example2_zh: 每位公民都应享有可靠的公共服务，不论收入多少或居住在哪里。
collocations: become a citizen｜成为公民 ; a senior citizen｜老年人 ; a responsible citizen｜负责任的公民
tip_zh: citizen强调公民身份；resident强调居住。

meanings_zh: n. 性格；角色 | n. 角色；人物 | n. 字符；文字
definition_en: personality; a person in a story | a person represented in a story, play, or film | a written or printed symbol, such as a letter
example1_en: Honesty is part of his character.
example1_zh: 诚实是他性格的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving historic buildings helps cities retain their distinctive character while adapting to modern economic demands.
example2_zh: 保护历史建筑有助于城市在适应现代经济需求的同时，保留自身的独特风貌。
collocations: main character｜主要角色 ; strength of character｜坚强品格 ; distinctive character｜独特风貌 ; Chinese characters｜汉字
tip_zh: 作“人物、字符”可数；作整体品质常不可数。

meanings_zh: n. 数字；人物 | n. 人物；人影；身形 | v. 认为；估计
definition_en: a number; an important person | a person, their outline, or the shape of their body | to think or decide something after considering it
example1_en: The figure on the board is wrong.
example2_en: Recent employment figures suggest that investment in public transport can create substantial opportunities for local workers.
example2_zh: 近期就业数据显示，投资公共交通能为当地劳动者创造大量机会。
collocations: sales figures｜销售数据 ; a leading figure｜领军人物 ; figure out｜弄清楚 ; a rough figure｜大致数值
tip_zh: 数据常用复数figures；figure out意为弄懂。

meanings_zh: v. 达到；完成
definition_en: to succeed in doing something
example1_en: He worked hard to achieve his goals.
example1_zh: 他努力工作以实现目标。
example2_en: Governments can achieve significant reductions in air pollution by investing in clean energy and improving public transport.
example2_zh: 政府可以通过投资清洁能源和改善公共交通，大幅减少空气污染。
collocations: achieve success｜取得成功 ; achieve a goal｜实现目标 ; achieve a balance｜达到平衡 ; achieve results｜取得成果
tip_zh: 直接接目标或成果，不说achieve to do。

meanings_zh: n. 习俗；习惯 | adj. 定制的 | n. 惠顾；光顾
definition_en: a usual practice | made to meet a particular customer's needs | the business customers give to a shop or company
example1_en: Shaking hands is a common custom.
example2_en: Schools can introduce children to local customs while encouraging respect for traditions from other cultures.
example2_zh: 学校可以向孩子们介绍当地风俗，同时鼓励他们尊重其他文化的传统。
collocations: local customs｜当地风俗 ; an ancient custom｜古老的习俗 ; custom furniture｜定制家具 ; regular custom｜经常光顾
tip_zh: custom指风俗或惯例；customs还可指海关。

meanings_zh: adj. 慷慨的 | adj. 充足的；大量的
definition_en: willing to give | larger or more plentiful than usual or expected
example1_en: She is generous with her time.
example2_en: Generous donations from local businesses can help community centres provide affordable activities for children and older residents.
example2_zh: 当地企业的慷慨捐助可以帮助社区中心为儿童和老年居民提供价格实惠的活动。
collocations: generous donation｜慷慨捐助 ; generous portion｜丰盛的一份 ; generous with your time｜不吝惜时间
tip_zh: be generous with sth表示在某方面慷慨。

meanings_zh: n. 气氛；大气 | n. 大气；大气层
definition_en: the feeling of a place; air around Earth | the mixture of gases surrounding a planet
example1_en: The classroom had a friendly atmosphere.
example2_en: A supportive classroom atmosphere encourages students to ask questions and participate more actively in discussions.
example2_zh: 相互支持的课堂氛围鼓励学生提问，并更加积极地参与讨论。
collocations: relaxed atmosphere｜轻松的氛围 ; create an atmosphere｜营造氛围 ; Earth's atmosphere｜地球大气层
tip_zh: 表示某种氛围常用an atmosphere；地球大气用the atmosphere。

meanings_zh: adj. 谦虚的；适度的 | adj. 适度的；不大的 | adj. 穿着端庄的
definition_en: not boastful; not large | not large in size, amount, or cost | wearing clothes that do not reveal much of the body
example1_en: She is modest about her success.
example1_zh: 她对自己的成功很谦虚。
example2_en: Even a modest increase in public transport funding could improve services in rural communities.
example2_zh: 即使公共交通拨款只小幅增加，也可能改善农村社区的服务。
collocations: modest about one's achievements｜对自己的成就谦虚 ; a modest increase｜小幅增长 ; a modest income｜不高的收入
tip_zh: 形容人常指谦虚；形容数量常指不大。

meanings_zh: n. 证据 | v. 表明；证明
definition_en: facts that prove something | To show clearly that something exists or is true.
example1_en: There is no evidence of cheating.
example2_en: Governments should consider scientific evidence before introducing policies intended to improve public health outcomes.
example2_zh: 政府在推出旨在改善公共健康状况的政策前，应考虑科学证据。
collocations: strong evidence｜有力证据 ; scientific evidence｜科学证据 ; evidence of｜……的证据 ; provide evidence｜提供证据
tip_zh: 作名词通常不可数：一项证据用a piece of evidence。

meanings_zh: n. 方法；靠近 | v. 接近；靠近 | v. 着手处理；接洽
definition_en: a way of dealing with something | To move nearer to someone or something. | To begin dealing with something or contact someone about it.
example1_en: A new approach may solve the problem.
example1_zh: 新方法可能解决这个问题。
example2_en: A balanced approach to urban planning should consider both economic growth and the protection of green spaces.
example2_zh: 均衡的城市规划方法应兼顾经济增长和绿地保护。
collocations: an approach to learning｜学习方法 ; adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; approach a problem｜着手处理问题 ; approach someone for advice｜找某人征求建议
tip_zh: 名词“方法”后用to加名词或动名词；动词后直接接宾语。

meanings_zh: adj. 道德的 | n. 寓意；教训
definition_en: about right and wrong | a lesson about right and wrong learned from a story
example1_en: The story has a moral lesson.
example2_en: Companies have a moral responsibility to ensure that their suppliers provide safe working conditions.
example2_zh: 企业在道义上有责任确保其供应商提供安全的工作环境。
collocations: moral responsibility｜道德责任 ; moral dilemma｜道德困境 ; moral support｜精神支持 ; the moral of the story｜故事的寓意
tip_zh: moral指道德；morale指士气，注意拼写区别。

meanings_zh: v. 进行；指挥 | v. 传导热或电 | n. 行为；举止
definition_en: to carry out; to lead | to allow heat or electricity to pass through | the way a person behaves, especially towards others
example1_en: Scientists conduct experiments in the lab.
example1_zh: 科学家在实验室进行实验。
example2_en: Researchers should conduct thorough trials before recommending new treatments for widespread use in public hospitals.
example2_zh: 研究人员在建议公立医院广泛采用新疗法之前，应开展充分的试验。
collocations: conduct research｜开展研究 ; conduct a survey｜进行调查 ; conduct electricity｜导电 ; code of conduct｜行为准则
tip_zh: 动词重音在后；名词重音在前，英音/ˈkɒndʌkt/。

meanings_zh: v. 辩论 | v. 辩论；讨论 | v. 仔细考虑；权衡
definition_en: to discuss opposing views | To discuss a subject by considering different views. | To think carefully about options before making a decision.
example1_en: Students will debate the topic in class.
example1_zh: 学生们将在课堂上辩论这个话题。
example2_en: The debate over free public transport centres on its environmental benefits and the cost to taxpayers.
example2_zh: 关于免费公共交通的争论集中在其环境效益和纳税人需要承担的费用上。
collocations: public debate｜公开讨论 ; heated debate｜激烈的辩论 ; debate an issue｜讨论一个问题 ; debate whether to｜斟酌是否要
tip_zh: 动词可直接接议题；debate whether to表示权衡。

meanings_zh: adj. 有益的
definition_en: helpful
example1_en: Walking is beneficial to health.
example2_en: Access to green spaces is particularly beneficial to urban residents who have limited opportunities for outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 对于户外锻炼机会有限的城市居民来说，能够使用绿地尤其有益。
collocations: beneficial effect｜有益影响 ; beneficial to health｜有益健康 ; mutually beneficial｜互利的
tip_zh: 常接to或for，说明对谁或哪方面有益。

meanings_zh: n. 边界；界限 | n. 界限；限度
definition_en: a line that marks a limit | A limit defining acceptable behaviour or the scope of something
example1_en: Respect personal boundary at work.
example1_zh: 在工作中尊重个人界限。
example2_en: Clear boundaries between work and personal life can protect employees' mental health and reduce long-term stress.
example2_zh: 明确工作与个人生活的界限，可以保护员工的心理健康并减轻长期压力。
collocations: a national boundary｜国界 ; set boundaries｜设定界限 ; cross a boundary｜越过边界 ; push the boundaries｜突破界限
tip_zh: boundary 强调分界；border 常用于国家或地区边界。

meanings_zh: v. 试图；尝试 | v. 尝试；试图
definition_en: to try | To try to do something, especially something difficult.
example1_en: She will attempt to climb the mountain.
example2_en: Many cities are attempting to reduce air pollution by improving public transport and expanding cycling networks.
example2_zh: 许多城市正通过改善公共交通和扩展自行车道网络来尝试减少空气污染。
collocations: make an attempt｜作出尝试 ; attempt to do something｜尝试做某事 ; a successful attempt｜成功的尝试 ; in an attempt to｜为了尝试
tip_zh: 动词后接to do；名词常用an attempt at doing。

meanings_zh: adj. 焦虑的；渴望的 | adj. 渴望的；急切的
definition_en: worried; eager | Very eager to do something or for something to happen.
example1_en: She felt anxious before the test.
example2_en: Students may become anxious about their future when career guidance is unavailable at school.
example2_zh: 学校不提供职业指导时，学生可能会对未来感到焦虑。
collocations: anxious about｜对……感到焦虑 ; anxious to please｜急于讨好 ; feel anxious｜感到焦虑
tip_zh: anxious about表担忧；anxious to do常表急切。

meanings_zh: v. 奉献；专心于
definition_en: to give time or energy to
example1_en: She will devote more time to study.
example1_zh: 她将把更多时间用于学习。
example2_en: Governments should devote more resources to preventive healthcare rather than relying entirely on expensive medical treatments.
example2_zh: 政府应将更多资源投入预防性医疗，而不是完全依赖昂贵的医学治疗。
collocations: devote time to｜投入时间于 ; devote resources to｜投入资源于 ; devote oneself to｜致力于
tip_zh: devote…to中的to是介词，后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 适应；改编 | v. 改编；改装
definition_en: to change to fit a new situation | to change something for a different use or audience
example1_en: Animals must adapt to climate change.
example1_zh: 动物必须适应气候变化。
example2_en: Schools must adapt their teaching methods to meet the needs of students from diverse cultural backgrounds.
example2_zh: 学校必须调整教学方法，以满足不同文化背景学生的需求。
