collocations: adapt to change｜适应变化 ; adapt teaching methods｜调整教学方法 ; adapt a novel for television｜把小说改编成电视剧
tip_zh: adapt to后接名词或动名词；勿混adopt（采用）。

meanings_zh: adj. 以前的 | adj. 前者的
definition_en: previous | being the first of two people or things just mentioned
example1_en: He is a former student of this school.
example1_zh: 他是这所学校以前的学生。
example2_en: Former industrial sites can be transformed into public parks, improving urban environments and creating shared spaces.
example2_zh: 昔日的工业用地可以改建为公园，从而改善城市环境并创造共享空间。
collocations: former colleague｜以前的同事 ; former president｜前任总统 ; former industrial site｜昔日工业用地
tip_zh: the former 指两者中的前者，the latter 指后者。

meanings_zh: adj. 明显的
definition_en: easy to see or understand
example1_en: It is evident that she studied hard.
example2_en: The benefits of improved public transport are evident in cities where traffic congestion has decreased.
example2_zh: 在交通拥堵有所缓解的城市，改善公共交通的益处显而易见。
collocations: clearly evident｜十分明显的 ; become evident｜变得明显 ; evident from｜从……可明显看出
tip_zh: 常用It is evident that...表示显然……。

meanings_zh: adj. 足够的；适当的
definition_en: enough
example1_en: Food supply is adequate.
example2_en: Schools need adequate funding to maintain safe buildings and provide effective support for students with additional needs.
example2_zh: 学校需要充足的资金来保障校舍安全，并为有额外需求的学生提供有效支持。
collocations: adequate funding｜充足的资金 ; adequate preparation｜充分准备 ; adequate for the task｜足以胜任任务
tip_zh: 表示达到所需标准，不等于优秀；常接for或to。

meanings_zh: adj. 实际的；真实的
definition_en: real
example1_en: The actual cost was higher.
example2_en: Governments should measure the actual impact of transport policies rather than relying solely on predicted benefits.
example2_zh: 政府应衡量交通政策的实际影响，而不是仅仅依赖预期收益。
collocations: actual cost｜实际成本 ; actual results｜实际结果 ; actual size｜实际大小
tip_zh: actual指实际的，不等于表示目前的current。

meanings_zh: adj. 明显的；表面上的 | adj. 表面上的；看似的
definition_en: easy to see; seeming | Seeming to be true, though possibly not actually true.
example1_en: It was apparent that he was tired.
example2_en: Despite the apparent benefits of remote learning, some students struggle without direct support from teachers.
example2_zh: 尽管远程学习看似有诸多好处，一些学生在缺乏教师直接帮助时仍感到吃力。
collocations: become apparent｜变得明显 ; for no apparent reason｜无明显原因 ; apparent contradiction｜表面上的矛盾
tip_zh: 可指“明显的”，也可指“看似的”，须看语境。

meanings_zh: adj. 逐渐的 | adj. 坡度平缓的
definition_en: happening slowly | Rising or falling gently rather than steeply
example1_en: Progress is often gradual.
example2_en: A gradual transition to renewable energy can help communities adapt without causing sudden job losses.
example2_zh: 逐步转向可再生能源有助于社区适应变化，避免就业岗位骤减。
collocations: gradual improvement｜逐步改善 ; gradual change｜渐进的变化 ; a gradual slope｜平缓的斜坡
tip_zh: 强调变化缓慢、分阶段；副词形式为gradually。

meanings_zh: v. 假定；承担 | v. 承担；就任 | v. 呈现；具有
definition_en: to suppose; to take on | To take on a duty, responsibility, or position. | To begin to have a particular appearance or quality.
example1_en: Don't assume that everyone knows the rules.
example1_zh: 不要假定人人都知道规则。
example2_en: Policymakers should not assume that all households have reliable internet access or adequate digital skills.
example2_zh: 政策制定者不应假定所有家庭都有稳定的网络连接或足够的数字技能。
collocations: assume that｜假定…… ; assume responsibility｜承担责任 ; assume office｜就任
tip_zh: assume常接that从句，强调未经证实便认为。

meanings_zh: v. 采用；收养 | v. 收养 | v. 正式通过；采纳
definition_en: to take up; to take as one's own | To legally take someone else's child into your family. | To formally approve a proposal, policy, or rule.
example1_en: The school will adopt a new teaching method.
example1_zh: 学校将采用一种新的教学方法。
example2_en: Governments should adopt long-term strategies that improve public transport rather than simply building more roads.
example2_zh: 政府应采取改善公共交通的长期策略，而不是一味增建道路。
collocations: adopt an approach｜采用一种方法 ; adopt a policy｜采纳一项政策 ; adopt a child｜收养孩子 ; adopt a resolution｜通过决议
tip_zh: adopt是采用或收养；adapt是适应或改编。

meanings_zh: n. 权威；当局 | n. 当局；主管机构 | n. 权威人士；专家
definition_en: power to make decisions | an official body responsible for a particular area or service | a person with extensive knowledge of a particular subject
example1_en: The school authority made a new rule.
example1_zh: 学校当局制定了新规则。
example2_en: Local authorities should consult residents before introducing policies that significantly affect access to public services.
example2_zh: 地方当局在推出显著影响公共服务获取的政策前，应征求居民意见。
collocations: have authority to do something｜有权做某事 ; local authorities｜地方当局 ; an authority on｜某方面的权威 ; abuse of authority｜滥用职权
tip_zh: 表权力通常不可数；the authorities常指当局。

meanings_zh: n. 贡献 | n. 捐款；捐赠物 | n. 投稿；稿件
definition_en: something given to help | Money or goods given to support a person or cause. | A piece of writing supplied for a publication.
example1_en: His contribution to science was huge.
example2_en: Public libraries make a valuable contribution to lifelong learning by providing free access to information.
example2_zh: 公共图书馆通过免费提供信息资源，为终身学习作出了宝贵贡献。
collocations: make a contribution to｜为…作出贡献 ; a significant contribution｜重大贡献 ; a voluntary contribution｜自愿捐款
tip_zh: 常用make a contribution to；to后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: v. 欣赏；感激 | v. 欣赏；赏识 | v. 理解；意识到
definition_en: to value or be thankful for | Recognise and enjoy the value or quality of something. | Understand the importance or difficulty of a situation.
example1_en: I really appreciate your help.
example2_en: Policymakers need to appreciate the difficulties rural communities face when accessing healthcare and other essential services.
example2_zh: 政策制定者需要理解农村社区在获取医疗及其他基本服务时面临的困难。
collocations: greatly appreciate｜非常感激 ; appreciate your help｜感谢你的帮助 ; appreciate the importance of｜认识到……的重要性 ; appreciate art｜欣赏艺术
tip_zh: 可接名词或动名词，不接to do；感谢帮助用appreciate your help。

meanings_zh: adj. 准确的 | adj. 精准的；命中目标的
definition_en: correct and exact | able to hit or reach the intended target
example1_en: Give an accurate answer, please.
example2_en: Accurate information about air quality enables residents to make informed decisions about outdoor exercise.
example2_zh: 准确的空气质量信息能帮助居民在充分知情的情况下决定是否进行户外锻炼。
collocations: accurate information｜准确信息 ; accurate measurements｜精确测量 ; highly accurate｜高度精确的 ; an accurate prediction｜准确的预测
tip_zh: accurate强调准确无误；precise更强调细节精确。

meanings_zh: n. 自由 | n. 免受；摆脱
definition_en: the right to act freely | The state of not experiencing something unpleasant.
example1_en: Speech freedom is valued in many places.
example1_zh: 许多地方重视言论自由。
example2_en: Universities should protect academic freedom while encouraging researchers to consider the social consequences of their work.
example2_zh: 大学应保护学术自由，同时鼓励研究人员考虑其工作的社会影响。
collocations: freedom of speech｜言论自由 ; freedom to choose｜选择的自由 ; academic freedom｜学术自由 ; freedom from fear｜免于恐惧
tip_zh: freedom to do表示做某事的自由；from表示免受。

meanings_zh: adj. 基本的；根本的 | n. 基本原理；基础知识
definition_en: basic and important | A basic principle or skill, usually considered with others.
example1_en: Honesty is a fundamental value.
example2_en: Access to clean drinking water is a fundamental requirement for improving public health in disadvantaged communities.
example2_zh: 获得清洁饮用水是改善弱势社区公共卫生的基本条件。
collocations: fundamental to｜对……至关重要 ; a fundamental principle｜基本原则 ; fundamental change｜根本性改变 ; the fundamentals of｜……的基础知识
tip_zh: 名词通常用复数 fundamentals，表示基本原理。

meanings_zh: n. 事务；事件 | n. 婚外情；私情
definition_en: a matter or event | a romantic relationship involving someone committed to another partner
example1_en: Public affair need careful attention.
example1_zh: 公共事务需要认真关注。
example2_en: Schools can encourage young people to take an interest in current affairs through regular discussions of global events.
example2_zh: 学校可以通过定期讨论全球事件，鼓励年轻人关注时事。
collocations: current affairs｜时事 ; foreign affairs｜外交事务 ; a private affair｜私事 ; have an affair｜有婚外情
tip_zh: 表公共事务常用复数affairs，如current affairs。

meanings_zh: adj. 最初的 | n. 姓名首字母 | v. 用姓名首字母签署
definition_en: first | The first letter of a person's name | To mark a document with the first letters of your names
example1_en: My initial plan was wrong.
example2_en: Although the initial cost of solar panels is high, households may save money over the longer term.
example2_zh: 虽然太阳能电池板的初期费用较高，但从长远看，家庭可能节省开支。
collocations: initial reaction｜最初的反应 ; initial assessment｜初步评估 ; initial cost｜初期费用 ; initial stages｜初始阶段
tip_zh: 形容词通常放在名词前；姓名首字母常用initials。

meanings_zh: v. 宣布；声明 | v. 申报
definition_en: to state officially | to officially report goods, income or other required information
example1_en: The mayor will declare the festival open.
example2_en: Local authorities may declare a public holiday to encourage participation in an important community celebration.
example2_zh: 地方政府可能宣布放假一天，以鼓励民众参加重要的社区庆典。
collocations: declare a winner｜宣布获胜者 ; declare an emergency｜宣布进入紧急状态 ; declare goods｜申报物品 ; declare income｜申报收入
tip_zh: declare强调公开或正式宣布；海关申报也用此词。

meanings_zh: n. 数据
definition_en: facts and figures
example1_en: Scientists collect data from tests.
example1_zh: 科学家从实验中收集数据。
example2_en: Reliable data allows policymakers to assess whether environmental regulations are reducing pollution in urban areas.
example2_zh: 可靠的数据能让政策制定者评估环境法规是否正在减少城市污染。
collocations: collect data｜收集数据 ; analyse data｜分析数据 ; personal data｜个人数据 ; data protection｜数据保护
tip_zh: 日常常作不可数名词；学术语境也用复数谓语。

meanings_zh: n. 环境；情况 | n. 经济状况；境遇
definition_en: a condition around an event | the conditions of someone's life, especially their financial situation
example1_en: Under no circumstance should you lie.
example1_zh: 在任何情况下你都不该说谎。
example2_en: Schools should consider each student's personal circumstances when developing policies on attendance and access to learning resources.
example2_zh: 学校制定出勤和学习资源获取政策时，应考虑每位学生的个人情况。
collocations: under the circumstances｜在这种情况下 ; personal circumstances｜个人情况 ; unforeseen circumstances｜意外情况 ; under no circumstances｜绝不
tip_zh: 常用复数；under no circumstances置句首须倒装。

meanings_zh: adj. 精致的；脆弱的 | adj. 微妙的；需谨慎处理的 | adj. 精巧的；柔和的
definition_en: fine; easily broken | Requiring careful handling to avoid problems or offence. | Fine, subtle, or gentle in appearance, flavour, or smell.
example1_en: Handle the glass with delicate care.
example2_en: Tourism in coastal regions must be carefully managed to protect delicate ecosystems from lasting damage.
example2_zh: 沿海地区的旅游业必须得到妥善管理，以保护脆弱的生态系统免遭长期破坏。
collocations: delicate balance｜微妙的平衡 ; delicate fabric｜易损面料 ; delicate flavour｜清淡的风味 ; delicate negotiations｜需谨慎进行的谈判
tip_zh: 既可形容易损物品，也可形容需谨慎处理的问题。

meanings_zh: v. 区分；辨别 | v. 成为…的特征；使有别于 | v. 看清；听出
definition_en: to tell apart | to make someone or something different from others | to see or hear something clearly enough to recognize it
example1_en: Babies learn to distinguish colors early.
example1_zh: 婴儿很早就能学会辨别颜色。
example2_en: Students should learn to distinguish reliable evidence from personal opinion when evaluating information online.
example2_zh: 学生在评估网络信息时，应学会区分可靠证据与个人观点。
collocations: distinguish between｜区分两者 ; distinguish A from B｜把A与B区分开 ; distinguish yourself｜使自己出众
tip_zh: 常用distinguish A from B或between A and B。

meanings_zh: adj. 灵活的 | adj. 柔韧的；易弯曲的
definition_en: able to change easily | able to bend easily without breaking
example1_en: Keep a flexible schedule.
example2_en: Flexible working arrangements can help employees balance professional responsibilities with their family commitments.
example2_zh: 灵活的工作安排能帮助员工兼顾工作职责与家庭责任。
collocations: flexible working hours｜弹性工作时间 ; a flexible approach｜灵活的方法 ; flexible materials｜柔性材料
tip_zh: 既可形容安排灵活，也可形容材料易弯曲。

meanings_zh: n. 焦虑
definition_en: a feeling of worry
example1_en: Exam anxiety is common among students.
example1_zh: 考试焦虑在学生中很常见。
example2_en: Regular physical activity can reduce anxiety among students facing demanding examinations and uncertain career prospects.
example2_zh: 经常锻炼可以减轻学生面对高难度考试和不确定就业前景时的焦虑。
collocations: anxiety about｜对……的焦虑 ; reduce anxiety｜减轻焦虑 ; severe anxiety｜严重焦虑
tip_zh: anxiety about后接担忧的事情；形容词是anxious。

meanings_zh: n. 冲突 | n. 矛盾；抵触 | v. 相冲突；相抵触
definition_en: a serious disagreement | A situation where different needs or ideas cannot agree. | To disagree with or be incompatible with something.
example1_en: Talking can reduce family conflict.
example1_zh: 沟通可以减少家庭冲突。
example2_en: Economic growth can conflict with environmental protection when industries rely heavily on fossil fuels.
example2_zh: 当工业高度依赖化石燃料时，经济增长可能与环境保护相冲突。
collocations: resolve a conflict｜解决冲突 ; conflict with｜与……相抵触 ; a conflict of interest｜利益冲突
tip_zh: 名词重音在首音节，动词重音在第二音节。

meanings_zh: v. 广播；播放 | n. 广播节目；播出
definition_en: to send out by radio or TV | A programme transmitted through radio, television, or the internet.
example1_en: The match will broadcast live tonight.
example2_en: Public television should broadcast educational programmes that help children understand science and develop an interest in learning.
example2_zh: 公共电视台应播出教育节目，帮助儿童理解科学并培养学习兴趣。
collocations: broadcast live｜现场直播 ; news broadcast｜新闻广播 ; broadcast a programme｜播出节目
tip_zh: 过去式和过去分词通常都为broadcast。

meanings_zh: n. 功能；作用 | v. 运转；发挥作用 | n. 函数
definition_en: the purpose of something | To work or operate in the intended way. | A mathematical relationship assigning each input exactly one output.
example1_en: What is the function of this button?
example1_zh: 这个按钮的功能是什么？
example2_en: Urban parks serve an important function by providing space for exercise, relaxation, and social interaction.
example2_zh: 城市公园提供运动、休闲和社交的空间，发挥着重要作用。
collocations: perform a function｜发挥作用 ; function properly｜正常运转 ; function as｜起……作用 ; basic function｜基本功能
tip_zh: function as后接名词，表示起……作用。

meanings_zh: n. 关心；担忧 | n. 令人担忧的事；关注事项 | v. 涉及；使担忧
definition_en: a worry or interest | An issue that matters or causes worry | To relate to someone or something, or cause worry
example1_en: Health is a shared concern for all.
example1_zh: 健康是所有人共同的关切。
example2_en: Growing concern about air pollution has encouraged many cities to invest in cleaner public transport systems.
example2_zh: 人们对空气污染日益担忧，促使许多城市投资建设更清洁的公共交通系统。
collocations: concern about safety｜对安全的担忧 ; raise concerns｜引发担忧 ; a major concern｜一个主要问题 ; concern for others｜对他人的关心
tip_zh: concern about多指对事情的担忧；for常指关心某人。

meanings_zh: n. 缺席；缺乏 | n. 缺乏；不存在
definition_en: the state of being away | a situation in which something does not exist or occur
example1_en: His absence from class worried the teacher.
example2_en: In the absence of reliable public transport, many residents have little choice but to drive.
example2_zh: 在缺乏可靠公共交通的情况下，许多居民别无选择，只能开车。
collocations: absence from work｜缺勤 ; in someone's absence｜在某人不在时 ; in the absence of｜在缺乏……的情况下 ; leave of absence｜获准休假
tip_zh: 缺席某活动用absence from；缺乏某物用absence of。

meanings_zh: adj. 持续的；不变的 | adj. 恒定的；不变的 | n. 常数；恒量
definition_en: happening all the time | remaining the same over time | a value or quantity that does not change
example1_en: There is constant noise from the street.
example2_en: Maintaining a constant temperature in public buildings can improve comfort but may increase energy consumption.
example2_zh: 公共建筑保持恒温可以提高舒适度，但可能增加能源消耗。
collocations: constant pressure｜持续的压力 ; constant temperature｜恒温 ; remain constant｜保持不变
tip_zh: 可指持续发生，也可指数值不变，须看语境。

meanings_zh: adj. 人造的；虚假的 | adj. 不自然的；做作的
definition_en: made by people, not natural | Not sincere or natural in appearance or behaviour
example1_en: artificial light can hurt sleep.
example2_en: Excessive artificial lighting in urban areas can disrupt wildlife behaviour and reduce the visibility of stars.
example2_zh: 城市中过量的人工照明会扰乱野生动物的行为，并使星星难以看清。
collocations: artificial intelligence｜人工智能 ; artificial lighting｜人工照明 ; artificial sweeteners｜人工甜味剂 ; an artificial smile｜做作的微笑
tip_zh: artificial指人造的；artistic才是艺术的。

meanings_zh: v. 分发；分配 | v. 使分布；使散布
definition_en: to give out | to spread something over an area
example1_en: Volunteers distribute food to the poor.
example1_zh: 志愿者向穷人分发食物。
example2_en: Governments must distribute healthcare resources fairly so that rural communities receive the same quality of care as urban residents.
example2_zh: 政府必须公平分配医疗资源，让农村社区享有与城市居民同等质量的医疗服务。
collocations: distribute food｜分发食物 ; distribute resources｜分配资源 ; evenly distributed｜均匀分布的 ; widely distributed｜广泛分布的
tip_zh: distribute A to B 表示“把A分发给B”。

meanings_zh: v. 贡献；捐献 | v. 促成；是原因之一 | v. 投稿；撰稿
definition_en: to give for a purpose | To help cause a particular result | To write material for a publication or website
example1_en: Everyone can contribute to the project.
example1_zh: 每个人都能为这个项目做贡献。
example2_en: Limited access to affordable housing can contribute to social inequality and force workers to accept longer commutes.
example2_zh: 难以获得可负担住房可能加剧社会不平等，并迫使劳动者接受更长的通勤时间。
collocations: contribute to a discussion｜参与讨论 ; contribute to economic growth｜促进经济增长 ; contribute funds｜捐助资金 ; contribute an article｜撰写稿件
tip_zh: contribute to中的to是介词，后接名词或动名词。

meanings_zh: adj. 绝对的；完全的 | adj. 绝对的；不受限制的
definition_en: total; complete | not limited by conditions, rules, or other authorities
example1_en: He has absolute confidence in the team.
example2_en: Giving any single institution absolute power can weaken accountability and reduce public trust in government.
example2_zh: 赋予任何单一机构不受限制的权力，都可能削弱问责机制并降低公众对政府的信任。
collocations: absolute silence｜鸦雀无声 ; absolute certainty｜绝对肯定 ; absolute power｜绝对权力 ; an absolute necessity｜绝对必需的事物
tip_zh: 常表示程度已达极限，通常不用 very 修饰。

meanings_zh: v. 决定；测定 | v. 决定；影响结果 | v. 决定；下决心
definition_en: to decide firmly; to find out | To control or strongly influence what happens. | To make a firm decision to do something.
example1_en: Tests help determine your progress.
example1_zh: 测试有助于测定你的进步。
example2_en: Researchers must determine whether smaller classes improve learning outcomes before governments invest heavily in additional teaching staff.
example2_zh: 在政府投入大量资金增聘教师之前，研究人员必须确定小班教学是否能改善学习成果。
collocations: determine the cause｜查明原因 ; determine whether｜确定是否 ; determine the outcome｜决定结果 ; be determined to｜决心做……
tip_zh: determine whether 意为查明是否；后接从句。

meanings_zh: adj. 无辜的；天真的 | adj. 天真的；单纯的 | adj. 无恶意的；无害的
definition_en: not guilty; pure | Lacking experience or knowledge of unpleasant aspects of life. | Not intended to hurt, offend, or cause trouble.
example1_en: The child looked innocent.
example2_en: A fair legal system must protect innocent people while ensuring that those responsible for crimes face justice.
example2_zh: 公平的法律制度必须保护无辜者，同时确保犯罪者受到法律制裁。
collocations: innocent of a crime｜未犯某罪 ; innocent victims｜无辜的受害者 ; an innocent mistake｜无心之失
tip_zh: 表示未犯某罪用innocent of，不用innocent from。

meanings_zh: adj. 合适的 | v. 擅自占用；挪用 | v. 拨款；拨出
definition_en: suitable | to take something for your own use without permission | to officially set aside money for a particular purpose
example1_en: Wear appropriate clothes for the interview.
example2_en: Governments should provide appropriate training to help workers adapt to technological changes in the labour market.
example2_zh: 政府应提供适当培训，帮助劳动者适应劳动力市场中的技术变革。
collocations: appropriate for｜适合于 ; appropriate measures｜适当措施 ; appropriate behaviour｜得体的行为 ; appropriate funds for｜为……拨款
tip_zh: 形容词词尾读/ət/，动词读/eɪt/。

meanings_zh: n. 便利 | n. 便利设施；方便的事物
definition_en: ease of use | Something that makes daily life easier.
example1_en: Online shopping offers great convenience.
example2_en: Although online shopping offers convenience, it may encourage unnecessary spending and increase packaging waste.
example2_zh: 虽然网上购物带来了便利，但它可能助长不必要的消费，并增加包装垃圾。
collocations: for convenience｜为了方便 ; at your convenience｜在你方便时 ; modern conveniences｜现代便利设施 ; convenience store｜便利店
tip_zh: 表示“方便”通常不可数；形容词是convenient。

meanings_zh: n. 后果 | n. 重要性
definition_en: a result of an action | The quality of being important or worth considering.
example1_en: Every choice has a consequence.
example2_en: One serious consequence of rapid urban growth is increased pressure on public transport and housing.
example2_zh: 城市快速扩张的一个严重后果是公共交通和住房承受的压力增大。
collocations: as a consequence｜因此 ; face the consequences｜面对后果 ; of little consequence｜无关紧要
tip_zh: as a consequence of后接原因，意为“由于”。

meanings_zh: v. 放弃；遗弃 | v. 放弃；终止 | n. 放纵；无拘无束
definition_en: to leave or give up | To stop doing or pursuing something before it is finished. | A lack of restraint in expressing feelings or enjoying yourself.
example1_en: We had to abandon the plan after the storm.
example1_zh: 暴风雨过后我们不得不放弃那个计划。
example2_en: Cities should not abandon ambitious recycling programmes simply because initial participation rates are lower than expected.
example2_zh: 城市不应仅因初期参与率低于预期，就放弃雄心勃勃的回收计划。
collocations: abandon a vehicle｜弃车 ; abandon a plan｜放弃计划 ; abandon hope｜放弃希望 ; with abandon｜纵情地
tip_zh: abandon直接接宾语；名词常见于with abandon。
